target.title: feat(voice-call): support Twilio calls in IE1 and AU1
target.body:
AI-assisted: Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

The voice-call plugin always sends Twilio Calls API requests to `api.twilio.com`, which selects Twilio's default US1 processing Region. Deployments using IE1 or AU1 cannot create, update, hang up, or inspect calls in that Region because Twilio call resources are Region-specific.

Closes #95828.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one optional `twilio.region` setting with a closed `us1 | ie1 | au1` contract. OpenClaw derives Twilio's current canonical REST hostname internally:

- `us1` or unset -> `api.twilio.com`
- `ie1` -> `api.dublin.ie1.twilio.com`
- `au1` -> `api.sydney.au1.twilio.com`

Twilio requires an Edge label in non-US REST hostnames, but its CDN automatically selects REST API ingress; the Edge label is not a useful user-facing choice here. Keeping only `region` avoids invalid combinations and reduces the config surface.

The provider prepares one API target containing the account-scoped base URL and exact hostname, then reuses it for both form-encoded mutations and status lookups. This keeps each SSRF allowlist coupled to the request host without allowing arbitrary base URLs or wildcard Twilio hosts.

## User Impact

Existing US1 users see no behavior change. Users can opt into IE1 with:

```json5
twilio: {
  accountSid: "ACxxxxxxxx",
  authToken: "<IE1_AUTH_TOKEN>",
  region: "ie1",
}
```

Unsupported regions fail config validation. No migration is needed because the earlier `edge` proposal existed only in this unshipped draft branch.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test:extension voice-call` — 50 test files and 463 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:docs` — documentation formatting, Markdown lint, MDX, i18n glossary, and 4,469 internal links passed with zero errors.

target.title: fix(shell-utils): escape control chars instead of deleting them\n\nFi…
target.body:
Fixes #99552

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99552. `sanitizeBinaryOutput()` strips every ASCII control character with code point < 32 (except tab, newline, and carriage return). When exec output contains terminal control sequences — e.g. SSH banners with ANSI color codes, cursor movement, `BEL` (7), `NUL` (0), or other control bytes — the remaining printable text can become so short that the renderer falls back to binary/MIME placeholder rendering, making the result appear blank or as an image placeholder.

## Why This Change Was Made

Instead of deleting control bytes outright, the sanitizer now strips ANSI/OSC sequences first, then escapes any remaining C0 controls to readable `\xHH` form. This preserves human-readable context while keeping terminal escape noise out of the model-visible transcript.

Specifically:

- ANSI CSI (e.g. `\x1b[1;32m...\x1b[0m`) and OSC sequences (e.g. `\x1b]0;title\x07`) are stripped before escaping.
- Residual C0 controls such as `BEL` (7), `NUL` (0), and backspace become `\x07`, `\x00`, etc.
- Tab, newline, and carriage return remain unchanged.
- Format and Surrogate code points are still stripped as before.

The ANSI stripping logic reuses `stripAnsi` from `src/agents/utils/ansi.ts`, the same helper already used by session rendering and bash executor paths. This keeps exec and session rendering on the same ANSI transcript contract instead of introducing a second parser. The remaining C0 controls are then escaped so the user can see that terminal bytes were present without raw bytes polluting output or triggering a MIME fallback.

This is a conservative, backward-compatible change: printable output is unchanged, and terminal bytes are now either removed (ANSI) or made visible (residual C0) rather than silently deleted.

## User Impact

Exec results from SSH, `qm guest exec`, and other terminal-bearing commands will no longer disappear into blank/image placeholders just because they contained ANSI escape sequences or low ASCII control bytes. Users see the cleaned text and escaped residual bytes.

## Evidence

Unit tests (now includes ANSI/OSC stripping and residual control escaping):

```bash
$ pnpm test src/agents/shell-utils.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /media/vdc/study/op/openclaw

 ✓ |agents| src/agents/shell-utils.test.ts (31 tests) 118ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
```

Key assertions:

- `strips ANSI/OSC escape sequences before escaping residual controls`
- `escapes non-ANSI control characters to hex form instead of deleting them`
- `keeps output non-empty when only control characters are present`
- `escapes NUL bytes`
- `escapes residual controls after stripping ANSI sequences`

Real behavior proof via the actual OpenClaw exec runtime (`scripts/proof-exec-sanitizer.ts`):

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-exec-sanitizer.ts

=== Command ===
node -e "process.stdout.write('\x1b[1;32mHello from OpenClaw exec\x1b[0m\x07\x00\n')"

=== Exit status ===
completed

=== Aggregated output after sanitizeBinaryOutput ===
Hello from OpenClaw exec\x07\x00

=== Checks ===
Contains readable text: true
ANSI ESC stripped: true
BEL escaped: true
NUL escaped: true
```

This demonstrates the user-visible path: a PTY exec command that emits ANSI color + `BEL` + `NUL` is stored as plain text with residual controls escaped, not as a blank or image placeholder.

For comparison, the old sanitizer (before this PR) would have deleted the ESC/BEL/NUL bytes and left the ANSI payload fragments in the output; `scripts/proof-sanitize-binary-output.ts` shows that contrast on simulated SSH/PTY banner output.

Format / lint:

```bash
$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 \
    src/agents/shell-utils.ts \
    src/agents/shell-utils.test.ts \
    scripts/proof-exec-sanitizer.ts \
    scripts/proof-sanitize-binary-output.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.json \
    src/agents/shell-utils.ts \
    src/agents/shell-utils.test.ts \
    scripts/proof-exec-sanitizer.ts \
    scripts/proof-sanitize-binary-output.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ git diff --check
# no output
```

target.title: fix: make `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider` install never fail
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Solves issues where installing `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider` might fail if the current system is incompatible with the available `node-llama-cpp` prebuilt binaries and building the native bindings from source also fails.

[Setting `config.nodeLlamaCppPostinstall` to `"ignoreFailedBuild"`](https://node-llama-cpp.withcat.ai/guide/troubleshooting#postinstall-behavior) allows the package installation to complete in that rare case, while still allowing `node-llama-cpp` to try building from source later when it is first used.

## Why This Change Was Made

This updates the llama.cpp provider to `node-llama-cpp` v3.19 and configures its postinstall behavior to avoid blocking provider installation when the native fallback build cannot complete. The change keeps the normal install path unchanged for compatible systems, and only changes the failure behavior for uncommon environments where neither a prebuilt binary nor a build from source is available.

This also brings the provider onto the latest `node-llama-cpp` release, including upstream improvements such as optimized arm prebuilt binaries.

## User Impact

Users are less likely to have OpenClaw extension installation fail because of a native `node-llama-cpp` build issue on their machine.

On systems where the prebuilt binaries are compatible, users should see no behavioral change. On systems where installation previously failed during `node-llama-cpp` postinstall, installation can now complete, and any remaining native build issue is deferred until the llama.cpp provider is actually used.

## Evidence

Known install/update failures this is intended to prevent:

- #6834 reports a Windows install/update failure where `node-llama-cpp` could not load a compatible prebuilt binary, fell back to building from source, failed to install/use CMake, and then failed the no-GPU source build.
- #41706, #35181, and #34180 show additional Windows install failures in the same `node-llama-cpp` postinstall/prebuilt-fallback area.

Upstream `node-llama-cpp` documents this exact failure path: postinstall checks whether prebuilt binaries are compatible, falls back to building native bindings from source when they are not, and can fail if the machine lacks the required build tools. The documented `ignoreFailedBuild` behavior keeps the default postinstall behavior, but ignores a failed source build so installation can still succeed; first use of `getLlama()` will attempt the build again.

This PR does not make local llama.cpp usable on machines that still cannot load the prebuilt native bindings or build them from source. It makes provider installation/update resilient to those native fallback build failures, so the failure is deferred until the llama.cpp provider is actually used.

target.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.visibleReplies` is set to `message_tool`, the agent is expected to call the message tool to deliver replies. If the LLM forgets (a probabilistic event — the reporter saw it happen on the 8th turn after 7 correct deliveries), the reply was **silently discarded**: the substantive text sat in the JSONL transcript but was never delivered to the user.

The existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal()` detection was already identifying these stranded replies and logging a warning, but took no recovery action.

## Fix

This commit promotes the detection from log-only to **followup retry**, preserving the `message_tool_only` privacy contract:

1. **Gate room events**: Skip stranded reply detection for ambient `room_event` turns where `message_tool_only` is automatically set by the system. Silence on room events is intentional by design — the agent chose not to respond.

2. **Enqueue followup retry turn**: When a stranded reply is detected, enqueue a followup run whose prompt instructs the agent to deliver the captured text via `message(action=send)`. The agent itself calls the message tool, so delivery happens through the correct contract path — no suppression bypass, no privacy boundary crossing.

3. **Clear transcript/persistence fields**: The retry run explicitly clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` from the original followup run to prevent the original user prompt from hiding the retry instruction. The followup runner resolves `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text`, so a retained `transcriptPrompt` would cause the agent to see the original user question instead of the retry delivery instruction.

4. **No suppression bypass**: This does NOT mark payloads with `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or use `skipSuppressionCheck`. The `message_tool_only` privacy contract is fully preserved: delivery only happens when the agent explicitly calls `message(action=send)`.

Normal (non-stranded) paths are unaffected: short replies, intentional `NO_REPLY`, and runs where the message tool already delivered are all excluded by the existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal` guard.

### Why followup retry instead of bypass delivery?

The `message_tool_only` contract says: "no message tool call = private/silent". Auto-publishing stranded text would break this documented behavior. Instead, we give the agent a second chance to follow the contract correctly — like returning an undelivered letter and asking the sender to mail it properly, rather than opening and publishing it ourselves.

## Changed files

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — followup retry with cleaned transcript fields, room_event gate (+26/-3 net)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 5 new retry/gate tests replacing 6 bypass tests (-4 net)

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 47 | ✅ All pass |
| `private-message-tool-final.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ All pass |
| `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | 189 | ✅ All pass (unchanged, confirms no regressions) |
| `followup-runner.test.ts` | 67 | ✅ All pass (confirms followup queue compatibility) |

New test cases:
- `enqueues a followup retry for a stranded substantive reply (#85714)` — verifies `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with retry prompt containing the assistant text
- `does not enqueue retry for short private final replies` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry when the message tool delivered this turn` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry for room_event turns (#85714)` — verifies room_event gate
- `clears transcriptPrompt on retry to prevent original prompt from hiding retry instruction (#85714)` — regression test verifying `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` are all `undefined` on the retry run

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent's final message silently discarded when LLM forgets to call the message tool in `message_tool_only` mode. The fix enqueues a followup retry turn so the agent can deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, patched checkout at `9dc3c76dc3`.
- **Privacy contract preserved**: The fix does NOT use `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or `skipSuppressionCheck`. No payload is auto-delivered. The agent is re-prompted to call `message(action=send)` itself.
- **Transcript isolation**: The retry run clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` so the followup runner's `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text` resolution correctly uses the retry prompt, not the original user message.
- **Room event safety**: Stranded reply detection is gated by `sessionCtx.InboundEventKind !== "room_event"`, so ambient room events (where silence is intentional) never trigger recovery. Covered by dedicated test case.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, `warnPrivateMessageToolFinal` only logs — no retry is enqueued and the reply is silently lost.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  ✓ auto-reply agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts (47 tests) 1729ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  47 passed (47)

  ✓ unit-fast private-message-tool-final.test.ts (8 tests) 2ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  8 passed (8)

  ✓ auto-reply dispatch-from-config.test.ts (189 tests) 3770ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  189 passed (189)

  ✓ auto-reply followup-runner.test.ts (67 tests) 1710ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  67 passed (67)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: When a stranded reply is detected, `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with a retry prompt containing the original assistant text and instructions to call `message(action=send)`. The retry run has `transcriptPrompt: undefined` so the followup runner correctly uses the retry instruction. Short replies, already-delivered replies, room events, and runs with existing transcript prompts are all verified by dedicated test cases.
- **What was not tested**: Live end-to-end delivery through an actual channel — the test verifies that the correct followup run is enqueued with the expected prompt shape and cleaned fields. The followup queue machinery (`enqueueFollowupRun` → `scheduleFollowupDrain` → `runReplyAgent`) is a well-tested existing mechanism used for concurrent message queuing.

## Real behavior proof (end-to-end, qa-lab host runner)

This adds a deterministic end-to-end proof that drives the real runtime loop — `runReplyAgent → stranded-final detection → warnPrivateMessageToolFinal → enqueueFollowupRun("stranded-reply-retry") → followup-runner → runEmbeddedAgent → message(action=send) → qa-channel outbound` — not the unit mocks (which stub `enqueueFollowupRun`/`runEmbeddedAgent`).

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Under `messages.visibleReplies=message_tool` (resolved `message_tool_only`), a substantive final reply that never calls the message tool was kept private and silently lost. The fix detects the stranded final and enqueues exactly one bounded followup retry that re-prompts the agent to deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract; if the retry strands again, no second retry is enqueued.
- **Real environment tested**: macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, branch `fix/stranded-reply-pending-delivery-85714` at current HEAD `0469009210` (rebased on latest upstream/main; recovery default-off + collect-batching isolation + updated scenario). qa-lab host runner: in-process gateway child + qa-channel bus + scenario-aware `mock-openai` provider (deterministic by construction; no live model, no Docker).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ran the new scenario, PASS:
  ```
  node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite \
    --provider-mode mock-openai \
    --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-recovery \
    --concurrency 1 --fast
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: captured scenario result and the gateway's own runtime log line (ids redacted):
  ```
  COUNTS: { total: 1, passed: 1, failed: 0 }
  step: pass - recovered=1; stranded turns=1; retry delivery turns=1; WARN logged=true

  2026-06-06T06:31:23.411+08:00 [source-reply/private-final] agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
  ```
  Asserted from the live request/outbound capture:
  - Turn 1 request: `plannedToolName !== "message"` (long plain-text final, stranded).
  - Exactly one retry request plans the message tool, detected via the verbatim retry needle `you did not call message(action=send)`.
  - Retry delivery request: `plannedToolName === "message"`, `plannedToolArgs.action === "send"`, `plannedToolArgs.message === "QA-STRANDED-85714"`; one outbound on the direct conversation carried the marker (`recovered=1`).
  - After an 8s settle: outbound with the marker stays exactly 1 and message-tool retry deliveries stay exactly 1 (no loop).
- **Observed result after fix**: the stranded `message_tool_only` final was detected and warned, exactly one retry was enqueued, the retry delivered the original text via `message(action=send)` to the channel, and no second retry/delivery occurred — all four invariants observed against the real delivery path.
- **What was not tested**: not run against a live frontier model (deterministic mock by design, since a real model "forgetting" the tool is non-deterministic), and not on a real chat transport (Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord) — exercised on the in-process qa-channel bus; the `message(action=send)` → source-conversation outbound contract is transport-agnostic core auto-reply behavior.

Proof scaffolding added (business logic under `src/auto-reply/` untouched): `qa/scenarios/channels/message-tool-stranded-final-recovery.md` (new scenario) and `extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.ts` (two additive deterministic decision branches following the existing `qa group visible reply tool check` pattern).

Closes #85714







## Update — retry drain scheduling (follow-up)

Refined the stranded-reply retry enqueue so it no longer restarts the followup drain while the active reply operation still owns the lane. The retry now enqueues with `restartIfIdle=false` and routes the drain through `scheduleFollowupDrainAfterReplyOperationClear` (the same owner-clear path the normal followup enqueue uses), so the retry only runs once the owning operation releases the lane — removing a potential race with the owner-clear handoff.

target.title: fix(gateway): defer hot-reload restart when dist/entry.js is missing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pushing commits into a live production git checkout triggers the gateway's hot-reload while `dist/` is mid-rebuild. The watcher (`requestRestart()` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`) immediately sends SIGTERM to the current healthy child process without checking whether the replacement build is valid for the new checkout state. The new child cannot start → crash-loop until systemd's start-limit is exhausted (37-min outage, P1, issue #99603).

## Changes

Two guard points using `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs, resolveHead)` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`:

### Guard 1 — requestRestart()

Before sending SIGTERM, verify:
1. `dist/entry.js` exists
2. `dist/.buildstamp` git HEAD matches current checkout HEAD

If either check fails (mid-rebuild or stale build), skip the kill and log. The running process is already loaded in memory and continues serving traffic. Restart will trigger on the next relevant file change.

### Guard 2 — Exit handler

When a child exits with SIGTERM/143, verify build readiness before restarting. If the build is not ready (rebuild was interrupted), settle the watcher so systemd restarts the process tree cleanly rather than crash-looping.

### Scope

Partial mitigation — prevents the crash-loop but keeps the existing stop-then-start restart ordering. Issue #99603 should remain open for a transactional restart (build-then-swap). Competing PR #99610 targets the same root cause; maintainers should choose one canonical repair.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Command: `npx tsx proof/hot-reload-race-guard.proof.ts`

```
HOT-RELOAD RACE GUARD PROOF
 Hostname: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
 PID:      <pid>
 Timestamp: 2026-07-03 18:49:10

 ─── 1. Production code: isBuildReadyForRestart ───
   ✅ Imported from scripts/watch-node.mjs

 ─── 2. Pure function: entry.js + build stamp checks ───
   ✅ entry.js missing → false
   ✅ entry exists, no readFileSync → true (fallback)
   ✅ build stamp HEAD != git HEAD → false
   ✅ build stamp HEAD == git HEAD → true

 ─── 3. Real filesystem lifecycle ───
   ✅ empty dist/ → false
   ✅ entry.js exists, no stamp → false
   ✅ stamp HEAD matches git HEAD → true
   ✅ stamp HEAD != git HEAD → false (git push)
   ✅ re-synced stamp → true (rebuild complete)

 ─── 4. Source code verification ───
   ✅ requestRestart() uses isBuildReadyForRestart
   ✅ Exit handler uses isBuildReadyForRestart
   ✅ isBuildReadyForRestart is exported
   ✅ no polling (narrow fix)

 ─── 5-7. Tests + lint ───
   ✅ Tests 24 passed (including guard tests)
   ✅ All run-node + watch-node tests pass (no regression)
   ✅ Lint: 0 warnings, 0 errors

 RESULTS: 16 passed, 0 failed
```


### Lint + TypeScript

```
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ pnpm check:test-types
# no type errors in changed files
```

- Partial mitigation; issue #99603 should remain open for stronger fix

Removes repeated TCP free-port discovery implementations from root-owned tests, where small cleanup and error-handling differences made the same test contract harder to audit and maintain.

target.title: improve(ui): flatten chat tool-call rows into a scannable list
target.body:
Closes #99760

## What Problem This Solves

Tool calls in the Control UI chat render as heavily decorated nested cards: the `Activity: N tools` group draws a bordered card, every tool message inside it draws another bubble box, and the summary button on top adds an accent gradient, an inset highlight, and a `0 8px 22px` drop shadow. Long tool summaries wrap across several lines. Dense agent sessions become hard to scan — a single 8-tool activity group fills an entire viewport.

Part of the box stacking is a CSS ordering bug: `components.css` begins with `@import "./chat.css"`, so its legacy `.chat-bubble` and `.chat-tool-card` blocks load after `chat/grouped.css`/`chat/tool-cards.css` and override the intended `.chat-bubble--tool-shell` resets (`padding: 0; border: 0; background: transparent`). Each tool row therefore leaks a full bubble box underneath the summary pill.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tool rows are now flat one-line rows (chevron + tool icon + label + mono detail, ellipsized), the activity group header is a flat clickable row, and its body is grouped by a thin left rule instead of a card. Expanded tool detail keeps soft tinted input/output blocks without card chrome; canvas/document previews keep their frame because they embed external content. Error states remain explicit (red icon/label plus `Error` badge, error groups still auto-expand). The duplicated legacy chat-bubble/tool-card CSS in `components.css` is deleted and the canonical `.chat-bubble` base in `chat/grouped.css` is reconciled to today's computed style, so normal user/assistant bubbles render unchanged. Dead render paths (`renderToolCardSidebar`, never-taken `renderToolDataBlock` branches) and their orphaned CSS are removed.

## User Impact

Chat sessions with tool activity are dramatically denser and calmer: an 8-tool activity group shrinks from roughly a full screen of stacked cards to a few compact rows, in both light and dark themes. Collapsed rows clamp to one line; the full command and output remain one click away. No behavior changes: expand/collapse, error badges, sidebar open, and previews all work as before.

target.title: fix: same-session inferred commitments can be starved indefinitely when a normal HEARTBEAT.md...
target.body:
## Summary

Found one regression risk: same-session inferred commitments can be starved indefinitely when a normal `HEARTBEAT.md` task is due on every heartbeat tick.

## What ClawSweeper Is Fixing

- **Medium: recurring due heartbeat tasks can prevent same-session commitments from ever delivering** (regression)
  - File: `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:1024`
  - Evidence: `firstDueCommitment` is now only selected when `dueHeartbeatTasks.length === 0` (`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:1024`). When any task is due, `resolveHeartbeatRunPrompt` returns the task prompt with `hasDueCommitments: false` (`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:870`), so `dueCommitmentIds` is empty and the commitment is neither attempted nor delivered. The scheduler’s follow-up pass explicitly skips the default session key (`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:1866`), so same-session commitments depend on a later default heartbeat run with no due tasks. For a documented/common setup like `heartbeat.every: "5m"` and a `tasks:` entry with `interval: 5m`, `isTaskDue` is true again on every cadence tick because it uses `nowMs - lastRunMs >= intervalMs` (`src/auto-reply/heartbeat.ts:288`). The new test covers the first half of this state by asserting the due commitment stays `pending` with `attempts...
  - Impact: users with opt-in inferred commitments and an every-heartbeat task can stop receiving natural follow-up check-ins for that session until the commitment expires, despite docs saying due commitments are delivered through heartbeat for the same agent/channel scope.
  - Suggested fix: keep task turns tool-capable, but process same-session commitments in a separate no-tools turn after the task run, or add a commitment-only wake/path that bypasses task selection without mixing untrusted commitment metadata into the tool-capable task prompt.

target.title: fix(runtime): guard JSON.stringify against circular tool output
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`writeRuntimeJson()`, the runtime `writeJson` method, and the plugin SDK `createLoggerBackedRuntime` all call `JSON.stringify(value)` on arbitrary tool return values. Circular references cause `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON`, crashing the output path.

Improves on the contributor fix in #99490. The original fix used `String(value)` as the sole fallback, which ClawSweeper found can still throw for null-prototype circular objects (`Object.create(null)` with circular refs → `Cannot convert object to primitive value`).

## Root Cause

Three call sites in `src/runtime.ts` and `src/plugin-sdk/runtime-logger.ts` stringify unknown runtime values with unguarded `JSON.stringify(value, null, space)`:

| Call site | File | Line (HEAD) |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `createRuntimeIo().writeJson` | `src/runtime.ts` | 84 |
| `writeRuntimeJson` log fallback | `src/runtime.ts` | 116 |
| `createLoggerBackedRuntime().writeJson` | `src/plugin-sdk/runtime-logger.ts` | 31 |

`JSON.stringify` throws synchronously on circular structures, and there is no catch. The tool return value flows through these paths unchecked.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extracted a pure `safeJsonOutput(value, space?)` helper in `src/runtime.ts` that never throws:

1. `JSON.stringify(value)` — normal path
2. Catch → `JSON.stringify(String(value))` — handles ordinary circular refs
3. Catch → `"[unserializable]"` — last-resort for null-prototype objects where even `String()` throws

Key design decisions:
- **Serialization separated from I/O**: The helper returns a string; `writeStdout()` and `logger.info()` are called outside the try-catch. This preserves the existing EPIPE/EIO handling in `writeStdout`.
- **Shared across all call sites**: The plugin SDK `runtime-logger.ts` imports the same helper, so the three identical bug surfaces share one defensive path.
- **Nested try-catch, not replacer-based**: `JSON.stringify` replacer cannot intercept circular references (the engine throws before calling the replacer), so a catch-based fallback chain is the only reliable approach.

## Changes

- `src/runtime.ts`: +21/-9 lines
  - Added exported `safeJsonOutput(value, space?)` helper with nested try-catch
  - `createRuntimeIo().writeJson` → `writeStdout(safeJsonOutput(value, space))`
  - `writeRuntimeJson` log fallback → `runtime.log(safeJsonOutput(value, space))`
- `src/plugin-sdk/runtime-logger.ts`: +2/-1 lines
  - Import `safeJsonOutput`; `createLoggerBackedRuntime().writeJson` → `logger.info(safeJsonOutput(value, space))`
- `src/runtime.test.ts`: +48/-2 lines
  - 5 new `safeJsonOutput` unit tests + 6 `writeRuntimeJson` tests (rewritten)
- `src/plugin-sdk/runtime.test.ts`: +24 lines
  - 2 new tests for logger-backed runtime circular + null-prototype paths

## Evidence

### Verification environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| OS | Linux 4.19.112 x86_64 |
| Node.js | v22.19.0 |
| Vitest | v4.1.8 |

### Unit tests (15/15 passed, 7 new)

```
src/runtime.test.ts (11 tests)
 ✓ safeJsonOutput > serializes plain objects with default spacing
 ✓ safeJsonOutput > serializes compact without space
 ✓ safeJsonOutput > serializes with custom space
 ✓ safeJsonOutput > falls back to String(value) for circular references
 ✓ safeJsonOutput > falls back to constant for null-prototype circular references
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > serializes plain objects via writeJson
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > handles circular references via writeJson
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > handles null-prototype circular references via writeJson
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > delegates to runtime.log when writeStdout is absent
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > falls back to String(value) in log path for circular references
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > falls back to constant in log path for null-prototype circular references

src/plugin-sdk/runtime.test.ts (4 tests)
 ✓ resolveRuntimeEnv > returns provided runtime when present
 ✓ resolveRuntimeEnv > creates logger-backed runtime when runtime is missing
 ✓ resolveRuntimeEnv > handles circular references in logger-backed writeJson  ← NEW
 ✓ resolveRuntimeEnv > handles null-prototype circular in logger-backed writeJson  ← NEW
```

### Real-process proof: all 5 code paths (production code, no mocking)

Standalone script imports the production `safeJsonOutput`, `createNonExitingRuntime`, `writeRuntimeJson`, and `createLoggerBackedRuntime` via `tsx`. No mocking — real Node process running the actual production code paths.

```

OpenClaw Runtime JSON Guard — Real-Process Verification
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PID:       <redacted>
Node:      v22.19.0
Platform:  linux x64

── Path A: safeJsonOutput (pure serializer) ──
  normal  : {"ok":true}

  Result:  PASS

}

  normal  : { "key": "value" }

── Path E: createLoggerBackedRuntime (plugin SDK logger) ──

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VERDICT
```

### Comparison: PR #99490 vs this fix

| Scenario | `main` | #99490 `String(value)` | This PR |
|----------|--------|------------------------|---------|
| Normal `{ok: true}` | ✅ JSON | ✅ JSON | ✅ JSON |
| Circular `a.self = a` | ❌ TypeError | ✅ `"[object Object]"` | ✅ `"[object Object]"` |

| Pipe error (EPIPE) | preserved | swallowed by catch | preserved |

## User Impact

- Prevents runtime crash when tools return objects with circular references
- The CLI outputs a safe fallback string instead of crashing
- Transparent to users; no config changes required
- Pipe-closed errors (EPIPE) continue to be handled correctly — the serialization catch does not interfere

target.title: fix(control-ui): improve session key display for direct chats with long identifiers
target.body:
Related: #61213 (partial fix — issue stays open for full priority scheme)

## What Problem This Solves

Long direct-chat session identifiers (e.g. `ou_67075ec667cac0a7feae2c5094fd27b2`, 30 chars; `user_1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef`, 36 chars) overflow the Sessions table cells and details panel in Control UI, making sessions hard to identify at a glance. Users on feishu/telegram/dingtalk direct chats with long open_ids see a wall of opaque characters instead of a recognizable session label.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scoped UI fix only — adds a dedicated `shortenSessionKeyForCell` helper in `ui/src/ui/session-display.ts`:

- Truncates identifiers >20 chars to `first_6...last_4` format (e.g. `ou_670...27b2`)
- Preserves full raw key in hover `title` attribute for debugging
- Keeps canonical `parseSessionKey` **unchanged** — no API/contract changes
- For non-direct keys (main/subagent/cron), defers to `parseSessionKey`'s fallback name directly (no prefix duplication)
- Applies only to Sessions table cell + details panel title

## Scope Clarification

This is a **partial fix for #61213**, addressing the immediate UI truncation need. The complete solution — full `binding.comment → agent.name → 技术标识符` priority scheme — is intentionally **out of scope** for this PR and should be tracked in a follow-up issue.

Issue #61213 stays open to track the complete priority implementation. This PR lands the user-facing pain point fix first.

## Data Model Compatibility

**No persisted/serialized state changes.**

- `shortenSessionKeyForCell` is a **pure display helper**, called only at render time in `renderRows()`
- `parseSessionKey` (canonical parser) is **unchanged** — same input/output contract
- No `JSON.stringify`, no `localStorage`, no config writes, no migration needed
- No upgrade impact — existing sessions render identically except long direct-chat IDs are truncated in display

## User Impact

- Sessions table cells no longer overflow horizontally
- Raw key still accessible via hover for debugging (no information loss)
- Identity rows (with `friendlyKeyLabel`) keep existing behavior — only fallback rows get truncation
- Short identifiers (≤20 chars) are unaffected
- Non-direct sessions (main/subagent/cron) render cleanly without prefix duplication

## Evidence

target.title: fix(ui): improve Thai locale copy
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: the new Thai Control UI locale still had high-visible English fallback copy and a few unnatural Thai labels around common controls, the agent detail surface, files, channels, cron panels, and the language picker.
- Why it matters: Thai users see these strings immediately after selecting Thai, and the docs/UI translation pipeline needs one shared terminology style.
- What changed: added Thai UI/docs glossary terms, updated Thai translation memory, regenerated `ui/src/i18n/locales/th.ts`, added a Thai copy regression test, and fixed the i18n generator process decoder so formatted multibyte locale output does not get replacement characters when stdout chunks split UTF-8 bytes.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no locale registry changes, no supported-locale changes, no docs generated-output edits under `docs/th/**`, no Mintlify/navigation behavior changes, and no public API or runtime contract changes.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #70510
- Related #3460
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Thai was recently enabled in the Control UI picker, but the Thai translation memory still carried English fallbacks and weaker terminology for high-visible agent/file/channel labels. While regenerating, the formatter subprocess output path could also decode UTF-8 chunks with `String(chunk)`, which can corrupt Thai text if a multibyte character is split across chunks.
- Missing detection / guardrail: existing i18n tests checked structural alignment and non-English fallback health, but did not lock specific Thai high-visible labels or replacement-character regressions.
- Contributing context (if known): #70510 tracks broader Thai docs feedback, so this PR intentionally updates glossary sources and Control UI copy without editing generated docs output.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: Thai common, language picker, agent, file preview, and cron delivery copy stays localized and does not contain the prior replacement-character corruption.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: these keys are generated output consumed directly by the Control UI, so a locale-level unit assertion catches both TM drift and generator corruption.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): structural locale alignment already existed in the same file, but it did not assert Thai wording quality.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Thai Control UI copy is more natural for high-visible labels such as Agent, Workspace, Tools, Channel, Default, Preview, language names, and file preview controls. Future Thai docs/UI translation runs also get the updated mixed technical glossary.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[select Thai] -> [agent/files/channels UI] -> [mixed English fallbacks and awkward labels]

After:
[select Thai] -> [agent/files/channels UI] -> [Thai localized labels using shared glossary terms]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26.4.1
- Runtime/container: Node v24.13.0, pnpm 10.33.2
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): Control UI i18n
- Relevant config (redacted): no translation provider configured; existing TM cache used

### Steps

1. Regenerate Thai Control UI locale from source translation memory.
2. Run i18n drift, targeted locale tests, docs glossary checks, formatter checks, and changed gate.
3. Inspect the generated Thai bundle for replacement-character corruption.

### Expected

- Thai locale bundle stays generator-clean, high-visible Thai labels are localized, and glossary source files stay valid.

### Actual

- Expected behavior confirmed locally.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Validation run:

```text
node --import tsx scripts/control-ui-i18n.ts sync --locale th --write
pnpm ui:i18n:check
pnpm test ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts src/i18n/registry.test.ts

pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 scripts/control-ui-i18n.ts ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts ui/src/i18n/locales/th.ts
git diff --check
OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK=1 OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK_MODE=throttled pnpm check:changed
```

Notes:

- `pnpm test ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts src/i18n/registry.test.ts` passed 2 Vitest shards: 81 UI files / 786 UI tests and 1 unit-fast file / 3 tests.
- `pnpm check:changed` selected core, coreTests, docs, and tooling lanes and completed successfully.
- Blacksmith Testbox was not run because the local `blacksmith` CLI is not installed. The unpinned remote installer was not executed; the local changed gate above was used as the fallback.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: regenerated Thai locale from TM, verified `ui:i18n:check` clean for all locales, verified Thai high-visible copy assertions, verified docs Thai glossary source check, verified no replacement characters remain in the Thai locale/TM, and verified local changed gate.
- Edge cases checked: UTF-8 multibyte formatter output from the i18n generator, language picker Thai/English labels, agent workspace/file preview labels, and cron delivery summary label.
- What you did **not** verify: browser screenshot of the Control UI and Blacksmith Testbox, because the Blacksmith CLI was unavailable locally.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) No
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Thai wording preferences can be subjective.
  - Mitigation: kept the scope to high-visible UI labels and encoded the mixed technical style in both UI and docs glossaries so future translation passes stay consistent.
- Risk: generator script change touches shared tooling.
  - Mitigation: narrowed the change to UTF-8 stream decoding for subprocess output and covered the observed Thai replacement-character failure with a locale test plus `ui:i18n:check`.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Thai Control UI high-visible labels now load from the regenerated Thai locale bundle with localized agent, workspace, channel, file-preview, and language picker copy instead of the prior English/awkward fallback wording.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS 26.4.1 with Node v24.13.0 and pnpm 10.33.2, using the generated `ui/src/i18n/locales/th.ts` bundle after the patch.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Loaded the generated Thai Control UI locale bundle with Node/tsx and printed the labels a Thai user would see in the agent/file/language picker surfaces.
- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal output from a live `node` locale import in this OpenClaw checkout:

```text
node --import tsx -e "import { th } from \"./ui/src/i18n/locales/th.ts\"; const proof = { commonDefault: th.agents.default, agentTabsTools: th.agents.tabs.tools, agentChannelsTitle: th.agents.channels.title, agentWorkspace: th.agents.context.workspace, filePreview: th.agents.files.preview, fileEmptyDraft: th.agents.files.emptyDraft, thaiLanguageLabel: th.languages.th }; console.log(JSON.stringify(proof, null, 2));"
{

  "agentTabsTools": "เครื่องมือ",
  "agentChannelsTitle": "ช่องทาง",
  "agentWorkspace": "เวิร์กสเปซ",
  "filePreview": "ดูตัวอย่าง",
  "fileEmptyDraft": "ร่างว่าง",

```

- **Observed result after fix**: The generated Thai bundle returns localized Thai strings for the visible Agent/Tools/Channel/Workspace/File Preview/Thai language labels, with no replacement-character corruption in the sampled output.
- **What was not tested**: Browser screenshot of the Control UI and Blacksmith Testbox, because the local `blacksmith` and `crabbox` CLIs are not installed in this environment.

target.title: fix: macOS-only Parallels smoke harness regression
target.body:
## Summary

Found one macOS-only Parallels smoke harness regression. The new guest script writer creates a root-owned `700` script, then the macOS lane executes it as the desktop user.

## What ClawSweeper Is Fixing

- **Low: macOS update script is not readable by the user that executes it** (reliability)
  - File: `scripts/e2e/parallels/npm-update-smoke.ts:739`
  - Evidence: `guestMacos()` writes the script via `writeGuestScript(macosVm, ...)`, then runs it through `prlctl exec ... --current-user ... /bin/bash <scriptPath>` or the sudo desktop-user fallback at lines 451-453. But `writeGuestScript()` writes with plain `prlctl exec <vm> /usr/bin/tee <scriptPath>` and then `chmod 700 <scriptPath>` at lines 730-739. The Parallels docs describe `--current-user` as logging in as the current guest OS user, so the write path and execute path are different identities for the macOS lane. ([docs.parallels.com](https://docs.parallels.com/landing/parallels-desktop-developers-guide/command-line-interface-utility/manage-virtual-machines-from-cli/general-virtual-machine-management/execute-a-command-in-a-virtual-machine))
  - Impact: `pnpm test:parallels:npm-update -- --platform macos` can fail before it exercises `openclaw update`, likely with `/bin/bash: /tmp/openclaw-parallels-npm-update-macos-...sh: Permission denied`. That breaks the intended release/update smoke coverage on current `main`; no later commit in the touched files fixes it.
  - Suggested fix: for macOS, write/chmod the temp script through the same resolved transport used to execute it, or explicitly `chown` it to the resolved desktop user and keep permissions non-world-readable because the script embeds provider credentials. Keep the Linux root-owned path separate.
  - Confidence: high

## Expected Repair Surface

- `scripts/e2e/parallels/npm-update-smoke.ts`
- `scripts/e2e/parallels/npm-update-scripts.ts`

## Source And Review Context

- ClawSweeper report: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/blob/main/records/openclaw-openclaw/commits/af5a1fbddb14a1f1ef2f6e9f3487f108d54ce066.md

- Latest main at intake: e311ffdcb94e760796a0a8a2c7e58fb8223678bf
- Original commit author: Peter Steinberger

- Review confidence: high

- Diff: `231e5c618f8ae700d51d080e4182a57588da888b..af5a1fbddb14a1f1ef2f6e9f3487f108d54ce066`
- Changed files: `scripts/e2e/parallels/npm-update-scripts.ts`, `scripts/e2e/parallels/npm-update-smoke.ts`

target.title: feat(feishu): add segment streaming mode
target.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in Feishu streaming delivery mode that accumulates model output and flushes complete segments at pause points, without changing the existing CardKit streaming-card default.

## Motivation

Feishu currently uses `channels.feishu.streaming` for CardKit live streaming. That behavior is useful when users want one live card that updates as the model generates text.

Some workflows need a different delivery style: show completed model text before a tool call, keep tool/status output in order, and then send the follow-up answer after the model resumes. Sending these boundaries as complete segments avoids sentence-by-sentence card updates while still giving users useful progress before the final reply.

## Configuration Behavior

`streaming` remains the top-level enable/disable switch for Feishu streaming delivery. `streamingMode` only applies when `streaming` is enabled.

| `streaming` | `streamingMode` | Behavior                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `false`     | `"card"`        | Streaming is disabled. Feishu sends replies through the regular non-streaming path; the mode value is ignored.                                          |
| `false`     | `"segment"`     | Streaming is disabled. Partial text is not accumulated and pause-point segment flushing is not enabled; the mode value is ignored.                      |
| `true`      | `"card"`        | Existing CardKit streaming behavior. Feishu updates one live card and closes it with the final content. This remains the default.                       |
| `true`      | `"segment"`     | New pause-point segment behavior. Feishu accumulates partial text and sends complete segments on tool start, idle, block, tool payload, or final reply. |

`chunkMode` still applies after a reply or segment is ready to send. In segment mode, `streamingMode: "segment"` decides when to flush a semantic segment, then `chunkMode` decides whether that segment needs to be split by length or newline before sending to Feishu.

## Changes

- Add `channels.feishu.streamingMode` with supported values:
  - `"card"`: default, existing CardKit streaming behavior
  - `"segment"`: accumulate model text and flush at pause points
- Preserve current `channels.feishu.streaming` semantics:
  - `true` enables streaming delivery
  - `false` disables streaming delivery
  - default mode remains CardKit streaming
- In segment mode:
  - partial model output is accumulated
  - accumulated text is flushed on tool start, idle, block, tool payload, or final reply
  - duplicate final text after an idle flush is suppressed
  - segment sends are serialized so final/tool payloads cannot overtake an in-flight partial flush
  - each flushed segment independently uses `renderMode: "auto"`
  - mentions are attached only to the first text segment
  - reasoning preview callbacks stay disabled because segment mode does not use live cards
- Update Feishu config schema, generated config metadata, docs, and tests.

## Example

Use segment delivery with:

```json5
{
  channels: {
    feishu: {
      streaming: true,
      streamingMode: "segment",
    },
  },
}
```

Default behavior remains:

```json5
{
  channels: {
    feishu: {
      streaming: true,
      streamingMode: "card",
    },
  },
}
```

## Compatibility

- Existing configs that only set `channels.feishu.streaming` keep the same behavior because `streamingMode` defaults to `"card"`.
- `streaming: false` continues to disable streaming delivery regardless of `streamingMode`.
- Segment mode is opt-in and does not change CardKit streaming-card behavior.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Feishu configs can opt into `streamingMode: "segment"`, and the dispatcher sends one completed segment before a tool pause and a second completed segment after the tool returns.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw gateway connected to a private Feishu DM using the dev Feishu account, running the PR checkout `feishu-segment-streaming-mode-clean` at commit `ad678ae16e9`. Node.js `v22.22.2`; pnpm dependencies installed in `/root/.openclaw/workspace-dev/projects/fork-repos/openclaw`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: Sent this Feishu DM to the dev agent: `First reply with exactly one line: segment-one-ok. Then you must call a tool to check the current date or time. After the tool returns, reply with exactly one line: segment-two-ok.` The dev Feishu account was configured with `streaming: true` and `streamingMode: "segment"`.
- Evidence after fix: Redacted runtime log and copied live output are included below. Gateway journal shows `segment flush reason=toolStart` followed by `segment flush reason=final`; agent session output shows `segment-one-ok`, `toolCall: session_status`, and `segment-two-ok`.
- Observed result after fix: The live Feishu turn emitted `segment-one-ok`, paused for the `session_status` tool call, then emitted `segment-two-ok`. Gateway logs show two segment flushes for the same Feishu turn, first with `reason=toolStart` and then with `reason=final`, and the dispatch completed with `replies=2`.
- What was not tested: Broad multi-user/load behavior and media upload fallback in a real Feishu tenant were not tested in this live run; media fallback behavior is covered by the targeted Feishu dispatcher tests below.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this patch, Feishu had no `streamingMode: "segment"` branch, so this live turn would use the existing CardKit streaming-card/default delivery path instead of two segment flushes.

Copied and redacted gateway journal plus agent-session output from the live Feishu run:

```text

assistant text: segment-one-ok
toolCall: session_status
toolResult: ok=true, sessionKey=agent:dev:feishu:direct:<redacted_sender>
assistant text: segment-two-ok
```

target.title: Telegram: allow native channel commands in explicitly allowed chats
target.body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

- Problem: Telegram `channel_post` updates could carry regular text, but native slash commands such as `/status` were not authorized
correctly in channel relay setups.
- Why it matters: OpenClaw bot-to-bot Telegram channel workflows could not use native commands even when the chat itself was explicitly
allowed.
- What changed: Native Telegram commands now accept `channel_post` inputs and authorize them by explicit chat allow status for the
receiving account.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): This PR does not redefine sender-scoped `groups[chatId].allowFrom` semantics for `channel_post`,
because Telegram does not expose the originating human sender on that surface.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Integrations
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #49062

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Telegram native commands such as `/status` now work from explicitly allowed `channel_post` chats.
- Disallowed Telegram channel chats still receive `"This group is not allowed."`
- Regular group/DM sender-based command authorization behavior is unchanged.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:

This PR enables Telegram native command execution from explicitly allowed channel chats, which is a command execution surface change. The
risk is bounded by existing explicit chat allow checks. Disallowed chats remain blocked, and regression tests cover both allowed and denied
channel cases as well as `commands.allowFrom.telegram` precedence.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

OpenClaw version: 2026.3.13
Operating system: all OS
Install method: npm global
Model: gpt-5.4
Provider / routing chain: chatgpt oauth



### Steps

1. Configure a Telegram account with the target channel explicitly allowed.
2. Send /status as a channel_post in that Telegram channel.
3. Observe native command authorization and reply behavior.

### Expected

- Explicitly allowed channel chats can execute native commands such as /status.

### Actual

- Before this fix, the command was rejected or dropped on channel_post.
- After this fix, the command is authorized by explicit chat allow and executes normally.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios:
    - /status from an explicitly allowed Telegram channel now succeeds.
    - Disallowed channel chats remain blocked by chat allowlist checks.
- Edge cases checked:
    - commands.allowFrom.telegram does not block explicitly allowed channel_post commands.
    - commands.allowFrom.telegram does not bypass denied channel_post chat allowlists.
- What you did not verify:
    - Sender-scoped groups[chatId].allowFrom semantics for channel_post
    - Live plugin command behavior on Telegram channels
    - Webhook-specific Telegram deployment paths

## Review Conversations

- [ ] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for
maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (Yes)
- Config/env changes? (No)
- Migration needed? (No)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps:

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly:
    - Revert this PR, or disable Telegram native commands temporarily with channels.telegram.commands.native: false
- Files/config to restore:
    - extensions/telegram/src/bot-native-commands.ts
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for:
    - Explicitly allowed Telegram channel /status still returns "You are not authorized to use this command."
    - Disallowed channel chats start executing native commands unexpectedly

## Risks and Mitigations

List only real risks for this PR. Add/remove entries as needed. If none, write None.

- Risk:
    - channel_post authorization now uses explicit chat allow rather than sender-scoped identity.
    - Mitigation:
        - This is limited to Telegram channel_post, where Telegram does not expose the originating human sender.
        - Explicit chat allow is still required.
        - Regression tests cover both allow and deny behavior.
- Risk:
    - Future contributors may assume sender-scoped groups[chatId].allowFrom also applies to channel_post.
    - Mitigation:
        - Scope is explicitly documented in this PR.
        - A separate follow-up issue will track channel_post sender-scoped allowlist semantics.

target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint before building inbound context. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without adding repeated thread-history requests to normal same-session follow-ups.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts`: 72 passed; covers stable `route.sessionKey`, stored thread `sessionId` rotation, same-session no-refetch, and reset-session refetch.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Live proof: local Docker Mattermost Team Edition 10.11.21 at `http://localhost:8065`, with tokens and Mattermost ids redacted. The proof used real Mattermost REST auth, posts, and `/api/v4/posts/<root>/thread` through `monitorMattermostProvider`; a fake websocket only injected `posted` events into the monitor. The route/thread session key stayed stable while the stored thread `sessionId` rotated. Cold start included prior root/thread context, same-session server-only context stayed absent, and stored-thread-session reset included new server-only prior context:

```json
{
  "mattermost": "10.11.21 local Docker, token/id redacted",
  "routeSessionKey": "stable, redacted",
  "threadSessionKey": "stable, redacted",
  "threadSessionKeyStable": true,
  "storedThreadSessionIds": [
    "stored-session-before-reset",
    "stored-session-after-reset"
  ],
  "dispatchCount": 3,
  "firstColdStartContainsPriorThreadContext": true,
  "firstColdStartContainsRootContext": true,
  "sameSessionSkippedServerOnlyContext": true,
  "storedThreadSessionIdResetContainsNewPriorContext": true
}
```

target.title: fix(daemon): refuse duplicate launchd gateway managers
target.body:
Closes #97178

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running the gateway under a system-domain LaunchDaemon could later run `openclaw gateway install` from a user session and silently add a duplicate gui-domain LaunchAgent for the same gateway label and port. That duplicate manager setup can restart-loop the gateway and disconnect clients.

## Why This Change Was Made

The macOS launchd installer now checks for a same-label system LaunchDaemon before it writes or bootstraps the user LaunchAgent. If `launchctl print system/<label>` succeeds or a matching `/Library/LaunchDaemons/<label>.plist` exists, install refuses with recovery guidance instead of creating a second KeepAlive manager. This intentionally stays narrow and does not add full system LaunchDaemon install/stop/uninstall lifecycle support.

AI-assisted: yes. I understand the change: it adds a pre-write launchd conflict guard and focused mocked launchd regressions for the reported duplicate-manager path.

## User Impact

Headless macOS operators who already manage the gateway as a system LaunchDaemon get a clear stop-and-fix error instead of a second user LaunchAgent that can fight the system daemon on the same port.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: `openclaw gateway install` refuses to write/bootstrap a gui-domain LaunchAgent when a same-label system LaunchDaemon is loaded or present on disk.

Real environment tested: local source checkout with mocked launchd states; the issue reporter supplied live headless macOS LaunchDaemon evidence on #97178. I did not mutate a real system LaunchDaemon on this host.

Exact steps:

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/inspect.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Evidence after fix: the new launchd tests cover both `launchctl print system/ai.openclaw.gateway` reporting a loaded daemon and `/Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` existing when the system job is not printed.

Observed result: focused launchd test passed; the broader daemon/status proof set passed in 2 Vitest shards.

What was not tested: live install against a disposable headless macOS host with a real system LaunchDaemon, to avoid creating or disturbing host-level launchd services from this automation run.


---

**Runtime proof — captured before/after (negative-control harness, macOS, Node 22):**

Exercised end-to-end through the real `installLaunchAgent` → `writeLaunchAgentPlist` → `assertNoSystemLaunchDaemonConflict` → real `execFile` path; only the external `launchctl` binary is mocked (a PATH shim), plist writes go to a scratch `HOME`. Same harness ran on unfixed `main` and on this branch.

_Before — unfixed `main` (negative control):_

```
Scenario A (no conflict, proceeds)  : PASS
Scenario B (conflict, refuses)      : FAIL
>>> UNFIXED: with a same-label system LaunchDaemon present, install did NOT
    refuse and WROTE the gui LaunchAgent plist anyway.  (the #97178 bug)
```

_After — this branch:_

```
Scenario A (no conflict, proceeds)  : PASS
Scenario B (conflict, refuses)      : PASS
error (verbatim): Existing system LaunchDaemon system/ai.openclaw.gateway detected at
  /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist. Refusing to install a gui-domain
  LaunchAgent for the same gateway label because duplicate launchd managers can
  restart-loop the gateway. ... sudo launchctl bootout system/ai.openclaw.gateway ...
plist written : false
>>> FIXED: the guard refused the duplicate manager with recovery guidance.
```

**What was not tested:** a live install against a disposable macOS host with a real system LaunchDaemon over a live port; and the on-disk `/Library/LaunchDaemons/<label>.plist` branch (needs a root-owned path via `sudo touch`/`rm`) — it shares the same throw site as the proven `launchctl print` branch.


---

**Branch-(b) proof — REAL root-owned `/Library/LaunchDaemons` plist (addresses the "mock-backed proof" review note):**

Re-ran on macOS with a genuine root-owned `/Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` (`sudo touch`), and with `launchctl print system/<label>` forced to report NOT-loaded (exit 113) so the **only** conflict signal is the real on-disk system plist — the `launchctl` shim plays no part in the decision. This exercises the real `/Library/LaunchDaemons` filesystem check (`LAUNCH_DAEMON_SYSTEM_DIR`) end-to-end.

_PR branch (`9f0f82df78`) — exit 0:_

```
launchctl print system/<label> : NOT-loaded (113)  -> branch-(a) inert
real /Library/LaunchDaemons plist present : yes     -> branch-(b) is the signal
install threw  : true
error (verbatim):
  | Existing system LaunchDaemon system/ai.openclaw.gateway detected at /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist.
  | Refusing to install a gui-domain LaunchAgent for the same gateway label because duplicate launchd managers can restart-loop the gateway.
  | Keep the system LaunchDaemon, or remove it first with `sudo launchctl bootout system/ai.openclaw.gateway` and `sudo rm /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist`, then rerun `openclaw gateway install`.
gui LaunchAgent written : false
>>> FIXED: install refused via the REAL root-owned system plist (branch-b).
```

_`main` (`29f5e9d35c`, no guard) — exit 1, negative control:_

```
launchctl print system/<label> : NOT-loaded (113)   real plist present : yes
install threw  : false
gui LaunchAgent written : true
>>> UNFIXED: install IGNORED the real system plist and wrote the gui LaunchAgent anyway — the #97178 bug.
```

target.title: fix: keep OpenClaw control tools available when tool_search misroutes
target.body:
Closes #99464
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server workers could be told to discover OpenClaw session/control tools through `tool_search`, but `tool_search` could resolve a different connector universe and leave the worker without the OpenClaw delegation controls it needed.

It also avoids changing the registered `heartbeat_respond` schema between normal and heartbeat turns on a resumed Codex thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the small, stable OpenClaw control set (`agents_list`, `sessions_spawn`, and `sessions_yield`) directly available on every Codex app-server turn. Broad tools remain deferred behind `tool_search`, and `heartbeat_respond` remains deferred with stable registration across normal and heartbeat turns.

This keeps delegation controls reliable without making the entire OpenClaw tool catalog direct, and preserves the Codex app-server requirement that a resumed thread retain the same registered dynamic-tool definitions.

## User Impact

Codex app-server agents can reliably list agents, spawn subagents, and yield without depending on connector-oriented `tool_search` resolution. Existing deferred-tool behavior remains in place for the broader catalog, and heartbeat turns no longer risk a thread schema mismatch.

target.title: fix: keep text tool results ahead of stale media placeholders
target.body:
Closes #99241

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reading text-only tool output could see or receive model responses based on media-placeholder text such as `(see attached image)` when a replayed or transformed tool result carried stale image/media blocks alongside the real text.

The affected workflow is agent/provider-bound handling of tool results during transcript replay, compaction, and provider message conversion. The visible symptom is that a plain text tool result can be misrepresented to the model as an image placeholder.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit text in a `toolResult` now wins over stale media blocks across provider transforms. Media placeholder fallback is reserved for media-only tool results, while mixed text/media tool results preserve the text and suppress stale image/audio placeholders.

This PR is intentionally limited to the minimal functional fix and regression coverage. It does not include the optional default-off diagnostic tracing used during local investigation.

AI-assisted: prepared with OpenClaw subagents and reviewed manually before submission.

## User Impact

Users can expect plain text tool results to remain visible to the model as text, even if replay or provider conversion encounters stale media blocks from adjacent tool output. Media-only tool results continue to use the existing placeholder behavior for providers that cannot consume the original media.

Operators get a narrower, provider-level fix without a Control UI change, config change, migration, or new runtime option.

## Evidence

- Focused regression tests via the repository wrapper:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts src/llm/providers/tool-result-text.test.ts src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts src/llm/providers/google-shared.convert.test.ts extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts src/llm/providers/mistral.test.ts src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts`
