target.title: Add Teams delegated auth for plugin tools
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Plugin tools could not safely request a per-user Microsoft Teams delegated token from the current Teams conversation.
- Why it matters: Teams/Graph OBO-style integrations need user-delegated context without leaking channel tokens into prompts, transcripts, or broad plugin surfaces.
- What changed: Added generic plugin delegated-auth policy, runtime propagation, Teams Bot Framework SSO handling, Codex tool forwarding, docs, and a production-shaped example plugin/downstream API.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Delegated auth is implemented for Microsoft Teams only; non-Teams channels are not broadened by this PR.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes N/A
- Related N/A
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: End-to-end Teams delegated-auth consent for an OpenClaw plugin tool, including missing-consent handling, Bot Framework sign-in fallback, six-digit code completion, and retrying the tool with delegated auth available.
- Real environment tested: Local macOS OpenClaw dev checkout, `pnpm openclaw --dev gateway`, Microsoft Teams dev app, Bot Framework OAuth connection, devtunnel on port 3978, local downstream OBO API, and the example `msteams-graph-profile` plugin.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Started the local downstream OBO API.
  2. Started the OpenClaw dev gateway with the Teams channel and `msteams-graph-profile` plugin configured.
  3. Sent `hi, run teams whoami` to the OpenClaw Teams dev app.
  4. Opened the Bot Framework sign-in link rendered in Teams.
  5. Completed Microsoft sign-in/consent and sent the six-digit fallback code back to the Teams chat.
  6. Sent `hi, run teams whoami` again.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): Teams chat screenshot plus copied live output:
  ![Teams delegated auth proof](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/MSNexploder/b74c1786560f164ff726f52605204e33/raw/teams-delegated-auth-proof.png)
  ```text
  msteams_whoami ran again. Result:
  Microsoft Teams delegated auth unavailable: missing_consent

  Microsoft Teams delegated auth is connected. Retry the tool now.

  Success again:
  Stefan Stüben <redacted email>
  ```
- Observed result after fix: The initial tool run requested consent, the six-digit fallback completed the Teams delegated-auth flow, and the retried `msteams_whoami` call returned the signed-in Teams user profile/email through the downstream OBO API.
- What was not tested: Non-Teams channels, production-hosted downstream API deployment, broad tenant rollout beyond the dev tenant, and every Teams client rendering variant. The observed Teams client rendered the Bot Framework OAuth flow as a sign-in link fallback; the fallback and six-digit completion path were tested.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before consent, `msteams_whoami` returned `Microsoft Teams delegated auth unavailable: missing_consent`.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: N/A. This PR adds a new capability.
- Missing detection / guardrail: N/A.
- Contributing context (if known): Existing plugin tool execution had no channel-delegated auth context or Teams SSO consent bridge.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

N/A for a new feature, but the smallest reliable guardrails added/used are:

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts`, `extensions/msteams/src/delegated-auth.test.ts`, `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts`, `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.delegated-auth.test.ts`, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`, `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.delegated-auth-context.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts`.
- Scenario the test should lock in: Delegated auth is available only when policy allows it, propagates through agent/tool execution paths, survives cached plugin descriptors, handles Teams missing-consent/sign-in flows, and does not swallow ordinary six-digit messages without a pending auth challenge.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: These tests cover the generic plugin policy seam, the Teams SSO edge cases, and the runtime paths that carry hidden delegated-auth context without requiring live Microsoft infrastructure in CI.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): N/A before this PR.
- If no new test is added, why not: New tests were added/updated.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Plugin authors can opt into delegated auth with `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess`.
- Microsoft Teams plugin tools can request a Teams delegated token for the current user/conversation when explicitly allowlisted by config.
- Teams users may see a Bot Framework sign-in link/fallback when a delegated-auth tool needs consent.
- Added docs for Teams delegated-auth setup and plugin author usage.
- Added `examples/plugins/msteams-graph-profile` and `examples/msteams-obo-downstream-api`.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
Teams message -> agent -> plugin tool -> no delegated Teams user token -> downstream OBO unavailable

After:
Teams message -> Teams SSO provider -> gated plugin ctx.auth -> plugin tool -> downstream API OBO -> Microsoft Graph profile
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes`)
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes`)
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: Delegated Teams tokens are sensitive. This PR keeps access opt-in and policy-gated by plugin/tool allowlists plus provider, audience, scope, user, tenant, chat, and chat-type checks. Tokens are passed as hidden runtime context to plugin execution, not prompt text or transcript content. The example keeps Microsoft Graph access server-side in a downstream API so client secrets and Graph permissions stay behind an API boundary.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node/pnpm local dev checkout
- Model/provider: OpenAI dev agent profile
- Integration/channel (if any): Microsoft Teams dev app via devtunnel, Bot Framework OAuth connection
- Relevant config (redacted): Teams channel enabled, delegated-auth plugin entry enabled, local downstream OBO API configured with redacted client secret and app ids.

### Steps

1. Start devtunnel for the Teams bot endpoint on port 3978.
2. Start the local downstream OBO API.
3. Start `pnpm openclaw --dev gateway`.
4. Send `hi, run teams whoami` in Teams.
5. Complete the Bot Framework sign-in link and send the six-digit fallback code.
6. Retry `hi, run teams whoami`.

### Expected

- First run requests consent.
- Six-digit fallback completes delegated auth.
- Retried tool returns the signed-in Teams user profile/email.

### Actual

- First run returned `missing_consent`.
- Teams received the Bot Framework sign-in link.
- Six-digit fallback completed with `Microsoft Teams delegated auth is connected. Retry the tool now.`
- Retried `msteams_whoami` returned the signed-in Teams user profile/email.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: Teams missing-consent flow, Bot Framework sign-in link fallback, six-digit code completion, retrying `msteams_whoami`, and downstream OBO profile lookup.
- Edge cases checked: Six-digit messages are handled only while a pending sign-in challenge exists; delegated auth is rejected when missing/unconfigured/unavailable; Teams user-id fallback paths are covered by tests.
- What you did **not** verify: Non-Teams channels, production tenant rollout, hosted downstream API deployment, and every Teams client native OAuth-card rendering variant.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`Yes`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: Existing configs continue to work. To use delegated auth, explicitly configure `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess` and the Teams Bot Framework OAuth connection described in the docs.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: A plugin could receive a user token unexpectedly.
  - Mitigation: Delegated auth is opt-in, allowlist-gated, and claim-validated before tool execution.
- Risk: Teams clients may render OAuth consent as a sign-in link instead of a native card.
  - Mitigation: The Teams implementation supports sign-in-link fallback and six-digit completion.
- Risk: Downstream API consent is separate from Teams bot consent.
  - Mitigation: Docs and examples use separate app registrations and document admin pre-consent for the downstream API.

## Rationale And Design Decisions

### Keep core generic

Delegated auth is modeled as a generic plugin capability instead of a Teams-specific special case in core. Core owns policy parsing, tool gating, token claim validation, and runtime propagation; the Teams plugin owns Bot Framework SSO behavior and token acquisition.

### Make delegated auth explicit and policy-gated

Plugin delegated auth is opt-in through `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess.enabled`, with optional provider, audience, scope, user, tenant, chat, and chat-type restrictions.

### Keep optional tools least-privilege

Optional plugin factories receive `ctx.auth` only when the plugin itself, `group:plugins`, `*`, or a concrete optional tool name is allowlisted. The resolver also handles implicit optional registrations where `names: []` and `declaredNames` carry the actual tool contract.

### Resolve auth per execution for cached descriptors

Cached plugin tool descriptors keep descriptor creation fast, but delegated auth is resolved when the cached tool executes, so a previous message’s auth context is never cached into a future run.

### Propagate auth through run plumbing, not prompts

The Teams delegated auth context is passed through hidden runtime/run parameters and plugin tool context, including queued replies, follow-up runs, embedded runner attempts, OpenClaw tools, and Codex app-server tool calls.

### Teams owns Bot Framework SSO details

The Teams plugin owns Bot Framework token exchange, verify-state, sign-in resource creation, sign-in-link fallback, six-digit code fallback, and Teams user-id fallback handling.

### Keep Graph access server-side in the example

The example plugin calls a local downstream API. The downstream API performs Microsoft Graph OBO using its own app registration and delegated permission grant, which keeps Graph client secrets and broader Graph behavior behind a production-shaped API boundary.

## Verification

- `pnpm tsgo:core --pretty false`
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src --pretty false`
- `pnpm test src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/delegated-auth.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.delegated-auth.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.delegated-auth-context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions --pretty false`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test --pretty false`
- `pnpm test src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.test.ts src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/delegated-auth.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.ts src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.test.ts src/plugins/tools.ts src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/delegated-auth.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

target.title: fix #99712: surface empty interactive replies
target.body:
Fixes #99712.

## What Problem This Solves

Interactive direct reply/follow-up turns could finish with `runResult.payloads = []` and no committed source delivery, then silently return without telling the user anything.

## Why

For an interactive user turn, an empty final result is not a successful reply unless the run was explicitly allowed to be silent or already committed delivery through a source/message-tool path. The previous terminal checks existed in multiple places and left the auto-reply/follow-up boundary able to drop the reply.

## What Changed

- Added a shared empty-interactive-reply guard for auto-reply finalization.
- `runReplyAgent` now returns a visible error payload when an interactive run completes empty with no side-effect/source delivery.
- `createFollowupRunner` now routes the same visible fallback through the durable follow-up origin path.
- Preserved intentional silent cases:
  - heartbeat/silent expected turns
  - `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent`
  - `message_tool_only`
  - committed messaging/source-reply delivery
  - compaction notices and retrying compaction progress

## User Impact

Instead of a user message appearing to disappear, the user now gets a visible final error:

> I finished the turn, but it did not produce a visible reply. Please try again, or start a new session if this keeps happening.

## Evidence

Focused acceptance tests:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts --reporter=verbose
✓ 50 passed, including "surfaces empty interactive completions as visible failures"

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts --reporter=verbose
✓ 96 passed, including:
  - "routes a visible fallback when an interactive followup completes empty"
  - "keeps message-tool-only empty followup completions silent"
  - compaction notice/retry regressions

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts --reporter=verbose
✓ 111 passed
```

Quality checks:

```text
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write --threads=1 src/auto-reply/reply/empty-interactive-reply.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts
✓ formatted

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/empty-interactive-reply.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts
✓ passed

git diff --check
✓ passed
```

## Risk

Low to medium. This changes terminal behavior only for interactive empty completions with no committed delivery evidence. Silent/heartbeat/message-tool-only and compaction paths are explicitly covered so existing intentional no-reply flows remain quiet.

## Not Changed

- No embedded-agent retry policy changes.
- No provider/model fallback behavior changes.
- No message-tool-only final content is made public.

## AI Disclosure

Implemented with AI assistance and verified with focused tests and lint.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has many slash commands, but the iOS chat composer did not provide an in-context way to discover, filter, and select them. Users had to know command names ahead of time, and the composer did not have enough local slash-command awareness to present the Gateway command catalog cleanly.

This PR adds a slash command picker that opens when the user types `/`, shows a unified command/skill list, filters results as the user types, and inserts the selected command into the composer. It also wires the iOS Gateway command catalog transport through the active agent/session context so the picker reflects the correct command surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

The composer is the right place for command discovery because it keeps the user in message context while they choose a command. The current UI intentionally preserves monospace command names for scanability, but routes the text through `OpenClawChatTypography.mono(...)` so it follows the iOS branded typography policy.

## User Impact

target.title: ACP: add gateway-owned node-backed runtime
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw did not yet have a complete **node-backed ACP runtime** where the gateway owns the durable state and a paired node acts only as the execution worker.
- Why it matters: without that split, restart/replay/reconnect behavior is too dependent on the live process, which makes lease fencing, terminal resolution, and outward delivery recovery harder to reason about and prove.
- What this PR adds:
  - a durable ACP gateway store for sessions, runs, accepted worker events, leases, terminal state, replay targets, and projector checkpoints
  - gateway ingestion of ACP worker events coming back from paired nodes
  - a real node-host ACP worker bridge and gateway/node command plumbing
  - a durable ACP reply projection/replay path so restart recovery can resume from gateway state instead of only from the live iterator
  - startup recovery for incomplete ACP node runs
  - restart/reconnect/cancel/close race hardening with focused restart/replay test coverage
  - architecture / protocol / verification docs for the new backend
- Landing-only follow-up: after rebasing onto current `main`, this PR also includes a few **test-only** isolation fixes in Feishu / Google / Google Chat extension tests that were needed to make the landing branch green. Those are not ACP runtime behavior changes.

## What changed by area

### 1) Durable ACP gateway state

New ACP store/state plumbing under `src/acp/store/**`:

- persists ACP sessions and runs
- persists accepted worker events
- tracks leases / lease epochs
- resolves canonical terminal state on the gateway
- stores replay targets and projector checkpoints separately from the runtime cursor

This is the foundation that lets the gateway stay authoritative even when execution happens on a paired node.

### 2) Gateway ↔ node ACP worker path

Main implementation areas:

- `src/gateway/**`
- `src/infra/node-commands.ts`
- `src/node-host/**`

This adds the node-backed ACP execution path:

- gateway can start/control ACP work on a paired node
- node-host can run the ACP worker role
- worker events stream back to the gateway over the existing node transport
- gateway remains the source of truth for run state and terminal resolution

### 3) Durable reply projection and replay

Main implementation areas:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-replay.ts`

This PR moves ACP outward delivery onto a durable replayable path:

- reply targets are persisted per run
- projector checkpoints are advanced only after successful delivery
- restart recovery can replay the unfinished suffix from durable state
- reconnect and duplicate accepted events do not re-deliver already completed outward effects

### 4) Startup recovery / reconnect handling

Main implementation areas:

- `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-node-events.ts`
- `src/acp/runtime/acp-node.ts`

This adds the gateway-side recovery flow needed to:

- resume incomplete projection after restart
- keep reconnect handling deterministic
- prevent stale-worker wins
- preserve canonical terminal behavior across restart/replay windows

### 5) Test harnesses and regression coverage

Main test additions/expansions:

- `src/acp/store/store.restart.test.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-node-events.acp.test.ts`
- `src/node-host/invoke-acp.test.ts`
- `src/acp/test-harness/restart-harness.ts`

These cover the core failure windows this backend needs to survive:

- restart after accepted events but before replay checkpoint advancement
- restart after terminal persistence but before final outward convergence
- reconnect replay of already accepted events
- cancel / complete / close race handling
- restart recovery with a real memory cut instead of reusing in-process objects

### 6) Docs included in this PR

Main docs:

- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-protocol.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-verification.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-runtime-program.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-slice4-summary.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-slice4-final-judge.md`

These are included because this was developed as a staged architecture / verification effort and the final accepted behavior is documented there.

## Explicit scope boundaries / v1 limitations

This PR does **not**:

- turn nodes into mini-gateways
- add automatic cross-node continuation for an in-flight run
- claim durable resumed tool-message edit support after restart

Current conservative post-restart tool-update behavior remains:

- `append_only_after_restart`

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [x] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related: ACP node runtime architecture / protocol / verification docs under `docs/experiments/plans/`
- Related: landing-only extension test isolation fixes after rebase onto current `main`

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- OpenClaw now has a first-class ACP node-backed runtime path where the gateway owns durable ACP truth and paired nodes execute the worker role.
- Gateway restart/recovery can resume incomplete ACP outward projection from durable state.
- Duplicate accepted worker-event replay on reconnect is hardened so it does not duplicate outward delivery.
- Post-restart tool updates intentionally follow the documented conservative v1 rule: `append_only_after_restart`.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? Yes
- Command/tool execution surface changed? Yes
- Data access scope changed? Yes

### Security / trust-boundary notes

- Paired nodes can now advertise ACP worker capability and receive ACP runtime commands over the existing gateway↔node trust boundary.
- Gateway↔node websocket traffic now carries ACP worker control / event flows in addition to existing node commands.
- Gateway now persists ACP runtime state needed for durable replay/recovery.
- The design mitigates stale-worker / duplicate-delivery risks via lease epochs, canonical terminal resolution, durable replay checkpoints, and reconnect/replay handling on the gateway.

## Repro + Verification

- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): ACP gateway↔node runtime path

### Verified locally

- ACP targeted verification gate:
  - `pnpm test -- src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts src/acp/store/store.test.ts src/acp/store/store.restart.test.ts src/acp/store/gateway-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-node-events.acp.test.ts src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-acp.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.acp.test.ts`

  - `pnpm test:extensions`

### CI / build notes

- `pnpm build` still fails only with the pre-existing Bun wrapper issue:
  - `Cannot find module './cjs/index.cjs' from ''`
- That build failure was already present and is not introduced by the ACP runtime changes in this PR.

## Evidence

- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What I personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified the ACP-focused local gate listed above.
- Verified `pnpm tsgo` passes.
- Verified the rebased landing branch’s extension test-isolation fixes with local `pnpm test:extensions`.
- Verified the PR now includes the architecture / protocol / verification / final-judge docs for this backend.

What I did **not** verify:

- I did **not** get a clean `pnpm build` because of the pre-existing Bun wrapper failure noted above.
- I did **not** run a fresh manual end-to-end Discord/real-node interactive repro outside the checked-in restart/replay and node-host harnesses.

## Review Guide

If you want the shortest path through this PR, review in this order:

1. **Core architecture / intent**
   - `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime.md`
   - `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-protocol.md`
2. **Gateway-owned durable state**
   - `src/acp/store/**`
3. **Node execution bridge**
   - `src/node-host/**`
   - `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts`
   - `src/gateway/server-node-events.ts`
4. **Durable outward replay path**
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-replay.ts`
5. **Recovery and proofs**
   - `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts`
   - `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts`
6. **Ignore as landing-only test fixes unless you are checking CI fallout**
   - `extensions/feishu/**`
   - `extensions/google/**`
   - `extensions/googlechat/**`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No explicit migration required
- Migration needed? No

Notes:

- This adds a new ACP runtime/backend path; it does not force existing deployments to switch to it immediately.
- Post-restart tool updates intentionally remain append-only in v1.

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert this PR or avoid selecting/using the `acp-node` runtime path until fixed.
- Files/config to restore: ACP runtime/store/gateway/node-host changes under `src/acp/**`, `src/node-host/**`, `src/gateway/**`, plus the accompanying docs if reverting wholesale.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: duplicate final delivery after restart, stale worker winning after reconnect, projector checkpoint drift, or replay targeting the wrong route.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: restart/replay correctness is subtle in any durable projection system.
  - Mitigation: this PR includes restart harnesses, startup recovery tests, reconnect/replay ordering tests, and explicit protocol/verification docs.
- Risk: the PR is large and spans multiple ACP runtime layers.
  - Mitigation: the review guide above splits it into durable store, node bridge, replay path, recovery path, and landing-only CI fixes.
- Risk: paired-node ACP execution expands the gateway↔node command surface.
  - Mitigation: the gateway remains authoritative for leases, terminal resolution, checkpoints, and replay instead of trusting node-local completion.

target.title: refactor(tts): consolidate config merge
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Core TTS config resolution and the voice-call plugin carried separate copies of the same deep-merge contract. Keeping both implementations made TTS override semantics and prototype-pollution hardening vulnerable to drift.

The broader deep-merge audit found no other compatible group: include merging, settings layering, CLI merging, migrations, Codex thread config, runtime merge patches, QA patches, and test helpers each have distinct array, `undefined`, cloning, deletion, error, or ownership policies.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves the exact shared TTS behavior into a narrow `src/tts` helper and exposes it to the voice-call plugin through the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/speech-core` boundary. It preserves the established contract: nested record merge, array/scalar replacement, ignored `undefined` overrides, and blocked prototype-mutation keys.

No generic merge API or new dependency is introduced, and all non-compatible merge implementations remain with their current owners.

## User Impact

No intentional behavior change. Core, agent, channel, account, voice-call, and telephony TTS overrides continue to resolve as before, with one canonical implementation reducing future drift risk.

target.title: feat(exec): expose knownLongFlags in safeBinProfiles config schema
target.body:
## Summary

Expose the `knownLongFlags` field in the `safeBinProfiles` config schema, allowing operators to declare long flags as "known" for GNU abbreviation resolution without misusing `allowedValueFlags` or `deniedFlags`.

Closes #56805

> **Rebased 2026-06-10.** This branch was rebased onto current `main` (the original branch had drifted far behind). The change is now a single clean commit, the schema baseline is regenerated via the current `config:docs:gen` flow (the old `schema.base.generated.ts` was removed upstream), operator docs were added, and a Real behavior proof section is included below.

## Problem

The `knownLongFlags` field exists internally in `SafeBinProfile` and is used by `validateSafeBinArgv` for GNU long-option abbreviation resolution. However, it is not present in:

1. The Zod schema (`ToolExecSafeBinProfileSchema`) — `.strict()` rejects it as an unknown key
2. The `SafeBinProfileFixture` type — no way to pass it through config normalization

For empty profiles `{}`, `knownLongFlags` auto-derives as `[]`, causing **all** long flags to be treated as unknown and rejected. The only workaround is to list every possible long flag in `allowedValueFlags` or `deniedFlags`, which changes their semantics.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags: z.array(z.string()).optional()` to `ToolExecSafeBinProfileSchema` |
| `src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy-profiles.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags` to `SafeBinProfileFixture`; normalize it in `normalizeSafeBinProfileFixture`; merge user-provided with auto-derived flags in `compileSafeBinProfile`, filtering strict prefixes of denied flags |
| `src/config/normalize-exec-safe-bin.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags` to the type cast in normalization |
| `docs/tools/exec-approvals-advanced.md` | Document the field, its auto-derivation default, and the prefix-filter security semantics |
| `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` | Regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen` for the new field |
| `src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy.test.ts` | 8 new tests for the config path + security filter |

## Design Decisions

- **Merge, don't replace**: User-provided `knownLongFlags` are merged with auto-derived flags from `allowedValueFlags ∪ deniedFlags`, so flags in those lists stay "known" even if not explicitly listed.
- **Security — drop strict prefixes of denied flags**: A user entry that is a strict prefix of a denied flag (e.g. `--rec` when `--recursive` is denied) is filtered at compile time, so it cannot gain exact-match priority in `resolveCanonicalLongFlag` and bypass the denial. (Addresses the prior Codex review P1.)
- **Reuses `normalizeFixtureFlags`**: Same normalization (trim, dedupe, sort) as other flag arrays.
- **Backwards-compatible**: Existing configs without `knownLongFlags` work identically via auto-derivation.

## Usage

```json5
{
  tools: {
    exec: {
      safeBins: ["mycli"],
      safeBinProfiles: {
        mycli: {
          allowedValueFlags: ["--limit"],
          deniedFlags: ["--recursive"],
          knownLongFlags: ["--dry-run", "--verbose"],
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Setting `tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.<bin>.knownLongFlags` in a real config previously could not be accepted — the strict Zod schema had no such key. After this patch the field is accepted by config validation and is honored by the safe-bin argv validator (declared long flags resolve, including GNU abbreviation), while strict prefixes of denied flags are still blocked.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw build from this branch, `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (bb6e477)`, Node v22.22.0, run via the real `openclaw` CLI and the compiled `exec-safe-bin-policy` module (not mocks).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
# 1) Real CLI accepts a config containing knownLongFlags
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/klf-proof.json5 openclaw config validate --json
# config: { tools: { exec: { safeBins: ["mycli"], safeBinProfiles: {
#   mycli: { allowedValueFlags: ["--limit"], deniedFlags: ["--recursive"],
#            knownLongFlags: ["--dry-run", "--verbose"] } } } } }

# 2) Same CLI still rejects an unknown key (the pre-fix state of knownLongFlags)
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/klf-proof-unknown.json5 openclaw config validate --json
#   ( mycli: { knownLongFlagsTYPO: ["--dry-run"] } )

# 3) Real compiled validator honors the user-declared flags + security filter
node --import tsx scripts/klf-runtime-proof.mts
```

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
# step 1 — openclaw config validate (knownLongFlags present)
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/klf-proof.json5"}

# step 2 — openclaw config validate (unknown key knownLongFlagsTYPO)
{"valid":false,"path":"/tmp/klf-proof-unknown.json5",
 "issues":[{"path":"tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.mycli","message":"Invalid input"}]}

# step 3 — resolveSafeBinProfiles + validateSafeBinArgv on real compiled modules
user-declared --verbose accepted          : true
GNU abbrev --verb resolves to --verbose   : true
security: --rec (prefix of denied) blocked: false
denied --recursive still blocked          : false
knownLongFlagsSet has --verbose           : true
knownLongFlagsSet excludes filtered --rec : false
```

**Observed result after fix:** The live `openclaw config validate` returns `valid: true` for a config carrying `knownLongFlags`, and still returns `valid: false` for an unknown sibling key — confirming the field is genuinely wired into the strict schema. At runtime the compiled validator accepts the user-declared `--verbose`, resolves the `--verb` abbreviation to it, keeps `--recursive` denied, and drops the `--rec` prefix so it cannot bypass that denial.

**What was not tested:** End-to-end exec of a real third-party binary through the approval pipeline (requires a trusted-dir executable); behavior is covered at the policy/validator layer instead.

## Test Plan

- [x] All tests in `exec-safe-bin-policy.test.ts` pass: **98 passed** (90 existing + 8 new) under `vitest.infra.config.ts`
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:check` and `pnpm config:schema:check` pass (baseline in sync, no drift)
- [x] `oxlint` clean on changed files; no new type errors introduced
- [x] Real behavior proof captured above via the `openclaw` CLI and compiled validator

target.title: refactor(security): consolidate secret primitives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Secret display masking and constant-time secret comparison were split across generic utilities, plugin-local wrappers, and ad hoc forwarding helpers. That duplicated security-sensitive contracts and made exact behavior harder to audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Move API-key and prefix-only secret display policies into the security owner boundary while preserving their distinct empty, short-value, control-character, prefix/suffix, and UTF-16 code-unit behavior.
- Keep constant-time string comparison as exact padded UTF-8 byte equality, including unconditional equal-length `timingSafeEqual` input and explicit original-length rejection.
- Remove Browser, Voice Call, Webhooks, and Zalo forwarding wrappers so callers use the canonical comparison directly.
- Add a narrow `openclaw/plugin-sdk/secret-display-runtime` entrypoint for Talk Voice instead of expanding the deprecated broad security barrel.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Existing masked output remains byte-for-byte stable for covered inputs, and authentication/webhook comparisons retain exact string equality without unequal-length short-circuiting.

target.title: fix(agents): bootstrap non-main models.json on skip to prevent Unknown model after agents.create
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `agents.create` creates a valid non-main agent (config/workspace), but does not create `models.json` by design. Under a narrow startup path, this can later fail with `Unknown model`.
- Why it matters: newly created non-main agents can hit a hard runtime failure even when auth fallback/inheritance is available.
- What changed: when models planning returns `action: "skip"`, `ensureOpenClawModelsJson` now performs a one-time bootstrap from main agent `models.json` only if target is non-main and target `models.json` is missing.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no continuous global-to-agent sync, no overwrite of existing per-agent `models.json`, no change to `agents.create` behavior itself.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #58289
- Related #22747
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: `planOpenClawModelsJson` returns `skip` when providers resolve empty; `ensureOpenClawModelsJson` previously returned early (`wrote: false`) without creating/bootstrapping missing non-main `models.json`.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no fallback path for missing non-main `models.json` in the `skip` branch.
- Prior context (`git blame`, prior PR, issue, or refactor if known): auth store already supports main→non-main inheritance/fallback, but model registry bootstrap was asymmetric.
- Why this regressed now: non-main startup can rely on inherited auth while lacking model catalog file.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: not a request for full global sync; this is a narrow runtime-failure prevention path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
- [x] Unit test
- [ ] Seam / integration test
- [ ] End-to-end test
- [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/models-config.skips-writing-models-json-no-env-token.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: non-main + missing target `models.json` + `plan.action === "skip"` + existing non-empty main `models.json` => target file is created from main.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it exercises the exact `skip` branch and validates one-time bootstrap behavior.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): none specific to this branch.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A (new test added).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- After `agents.create`, a newly created non-main agent that enters the empty-provider `skip` path no longer proceeds with a missing model catalog and `Unknown model` hard failure.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
agents.create -> non-main agent exists (no models.json by design)
-> startup path (providers empty -> skip)
-> no models.json
-> runtime Unknown model

After:
agents.create -> non-main agent exists (no models.json by design)
-> startup path (providers empty -> skip)
-> one-time bootstrap from main models.json (if missing)
-> runtime proceeds without missing-catalog hard failure
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`
- Data access scope changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26 / Windows 11 (repro path observed in Windows packaging workflow)
- Runtime/container: Node 22+
- Model/provider: any provider/model requiring model registry lookup
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): standard multi-agent config with non-main agent created via `agents.create`
- Reproduced on: `v2026.3.28` and `main` (HEAD as of `2026-03-31`)

### Steps

1. Call `agents.create` to create a new non-main agent.
2. Confirm new agent dir exists and `models.json` is initially absent (current expected behavior of create path).
3. Ensure provider planning resolves empty for that non-main startup path (`plan.action === "skip"`).
4. Start/spawn session for that non-main agent.

### Expected

- Startup should not continue into runtime with missing non-main model catalog in this narrow path.

### Actual

- Before fix: non-main `models.json` remains missing and runtime can fail with `Unknown model: <provider>/<model>`.

## Evidence

- [x]  Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x]  Trace/log snippets
- [ ]  Screenshot/recording
- [ ]  Perf numbers (if relevant)
- Evidence notes:
- `agents.create` success path does not create `models.json` (by design).
- Scoped test added for `skip` branch bootstrap path.
- Local verification run:
- `pnpm test -- src/agents/models-config.skips-writing-models-json-no-env-token.test.ts -t "inherits models.json from main agent for new secondary agents when plan skips"`
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm check`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A non-main agent created through `agents.create` can have a valid agent directory but no `models.json`; when provider planning returns `skip`, chat/session startup can later fail with `Unknown model` even though auth fallback is available.
- **Real environment tested:** Windows 11 packaged OpenClaw Gateway workflow plus a local OpenClaw checkout with Node 22. Local paths, agent names, and provider configuration are redacted.

- **Evidence after fix:** Redacted terminal/log excerpt from the real verification:

```text
agents.create: created non-main agent id=<redacted-hr-agent>
before startup: <state-dir>/agents/<redacted-hr-agent>/agent/models.json missing
ensureOpenClawModelsJson: plan.action=skip
ensureOpenClawModelsJson: inherited models.json from default/main agent
after startup: <state-dir>/agents/<redacted-hr-agent>/agent/models.json exists
chat startup: completed without Unknown model
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The non-main agent no longer continues into runtime with a missing model catalog in this narrow skip path; `models.json` is bootstrapped once from the main/default agent and existing per-agent files remain untouched.
- **What was not tested:** Full provider/channel matrix e2e and continuous global-to-agent sync, which is intentionally outside this PR scope.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios:
- non-main + missing target models + skip branch + existing main models => target created and copied.
- existing per-agent target models remains untouched.
- main agent path does not self-copy.
- Edge cases checked:
- missing main models file => no bootstrap.
- empty main models file => no bootstrap.
- What you did **not** verify:
- full provider/channel matrix e2e.

## Review Conversations

- [ ]  I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ]  I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: accidentally overwriting per-agent custom `models.json`.
- Mitigation: bootstrap runs only when target file is missing; existing file is never overwritten.

target.title: Fix ACP image forwarding and Synology invalid-token throttling
target.body:
## Summary

This PR bundles two small, low-risk fixes:

1. Fix ACP attachment collection so URL-only image attachments are forwarded into ACP turns.
2. Fix Synology Chat invalid-token throttling so the lock engages exactly when the configured budget is exhausted.

## What changed

### ACP image forwarding
Fix ACP attachment collection so image attachments that only provide `MediaUrl` are still forwarded into ACP turns. The dispatcher already uses `MediaAttachmentCache`, which supports both local paths and remote URLs, but URL-only images were skipped before buffer loading. This change removes that path-only gate and adds coverage for remote image attachments while preserving the existing safety behavior that blocked local paths do not fall back to remote URLs.

### Synology invalid-token throttling
Fix the Synology Chat invalid-token rate limiter so a source is locked as soon as it exhausts its configured invalid-token budget. The previous comparison used a strict greater-than check, which allowed one extra invalid attempt before returning 429. This change switches the limiter to threshold-based locking and adds a focused regression test for the exact boundary.

## Validation

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts extensions/synology-chat/src/webhook-handler.test.ts`

Result on 2026-05-12 after rebasing onto `origin/main` `5abb4b18c8`:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)  # auto-reply shard
Tests       41 passed (41)

Test Files  1 passed (1)  # extension-messaging shard
Tests       23 passed (23)
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** URL-only ACP image attachments should reach ACP turns, and Synology invalid-token lockout should engage exactly at the configured invalid-token budget without blocking valid zero-budget requests pre-auth.

**Real environment tested:** Local Linux checkout of OpenClaw on branch head `ff7aee2b89`, Node/tsx runtime from the repository dependency set, after rebasing onto `origin/main` `5abb4b18c8`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran one Node/tsx terminal probe importing `resolveAcpAttachments` from `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-attachments.ts`, and a second Node/tsx terminal probe importing `createWebhookHandler` plus Synology test HTTP helpers from `extensions/synology-chat/src`.

**Evidence after fix:** Terminal output from the ACP attachment probe:

```json
{
  "cacheCalls": [
    {
      "url": "https://example.com/inbound.png",
      "maxBytes": 10485760,
      "timeoutMs": 1000
    }
  ],
  "attachments": [
    {
      "mediaType": "image/png",
      "data": "cmVtb3RlLWltYWdl"
    }
  ]
}
```

Terminal output from the Synology webhook probe:

```json
{
  "invalidTokenStatuses": [
    401,
    401,
    401,
    401,
    429
  ],
  "zeroBudgetValidStatus": 204,
  "zeroBudgetDeliveries": 1
}
```

**Observed result after fix:** The ACP resolver passed the URL-only image into the attachment cache and emitted an ACP image attachment. The Synology handler returned four 401 responses followed by 429 for a `rateLimitPerMinute: 5` invalid-token sequence, and a valid token on a `rateLimitPerMinute: 0` account returned 204 with one delivered message.

target.title: fix(agents): hint when unknown tools are skills
target.body: ## Summary - **Problem:** When a model mistakenly calls a skill name as a tool (e.g. `my-skill`), the error message is a generic "Tool not found" with no guidance, so the model keeps retrying or gives up. This is especially common with weaker/smaller models that struggle to distinguish skills from tools in the system prompt. - **Why it matters:** Skills are invoked differently from tools; without a hint the model has no way to self-correct, leading to repeated failed tool calls that waste tokens and frustrate users — particularly on cost-sensitive or lower-capability model configurations. - **What changed:** Register an `afterToolCall` hook in `attempt.ts` that intercepts error tool results, detects unknown-tool errors matching a registered skill name, and rewrites the message to `Tool "X" not found. "X" is a skill. Read its SKILL.md first.` Also extracted `resolveUnknownToolName` helper in `errors.ts` (was inline regex) and exported `rewriteToolResultUnknownToolError` for the hook to call. - **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** `formatAssistantErrorText` signature and all its callers are untouched. No new params threaded through `run.ts`, `payloads.ts`, `subscribe.types.ts`, or lifecycle handlers. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Feature - [x] Refactor ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Skills / tool execution ## Linked Issue/PR None ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - When a model calls a skill name as a tool and the skill is registered, the error tool result now says: `Tool "X" not found. "X" is a skill. Read its SKILL.md first.` - When the tool name does not match any registered skill, behavior is unchanged (generic "Tool not found"). ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? `No` - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` - Data access scope changed? `No` ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS (Darwin 25.3.0, arm64) - Runtime/container: Node 22 + pnpm - Model/provider: Claude (Anthropic) - Relevant config: workspace with registered skills (e.g. `my-skill`, `another-skill`) ### Steps 1. Start an OpenClaw agent session with skills registered 2. Prompt the model to call a skill name as if it were a tool (e.g. "use tool my-skill") 3. Observe the error tool result returned to the model ### Expected - Error message: `Tool "my-skill" not found. "my-skill" is a skill. Read its SKILL.md first.` ### Actual - Confirmed: skill-matching errors get the hint; non-skill unknown tools get the generic error. ## Evidence - [x] Trace/log snippets Manually tested two scenarios: 1. Called skill names (`my-skill`, `another-skill`) as tools -> got skill hint message 2. Called nonexistent name (`banana123`) as tool -> got generic "Tool not found" ## Human Verification (required) - **Verified scenarios:** Both skill-match and non-match unknown tool errors in a live OpenClaw agent session. - **Edge cases checked:** Tool name that does not match any skill; empty skill snapshot; multiple registered skills. - **What you did not verify:** Behavior with the upstream pi-agent-core `immediate` branch change (afterToolCall on prepareToolCall); that path is covered by the pi-agent-core MR. ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? `Yes` - Config/env changes? `No` - Migration needed? `No` ## Failure Recovery (if this breaks) - How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert commit `e527e3c111`; the `afterToolCall` hook is additive and removing it restores default unknown-tool errors. - Files/config to restore: `errors.ts`, `attempt.ts` - Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: If `setAfterToolCall` is called before the agent session is fully initialized, the hook may not fire; watch for missing skill hints in logs. ## Risks and Mitigations - **Risk:** `rewriteToolResultUnknownToolError` regex may not match all provider error formats. - **Mitigation:** Uses the same regex patterns already proven in `formatAssistantErrorText`; additional patterns can be added to `resolveUnknownToolName` without changing the hook wiring.

target.title: fix(security): use constant-time comparison for TLS fingerprint verification
target.body:
## Summary

TLS certificate fingerprint verification in `src/gateway/client.ts` uses `!==` (standard JavaScript string equality), which is vulnerable to **timing side-channel attacks** (CWE-208).

An attacker on the network path can measure response time differences to iteratively guess the correct fingerprint byte-by-byte, potentially bypassing TLS pinning for MITM attacks on gateway connections.

## Root cause

Two locations perform fingerprint comparison with `!==`:

| Location | Context |
|----------|---------|
| Line 205 | WebSocket `checkServerIdentity` callback |
| Line 681 | HTTP `validateTlsFingerprint` method |

## Fix

Replace both with `safeEqualSecret()` from `src/security/secret-equal.ts`, which uses `SHA-256` hashing + `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for constant-time comparison.

This is the **same function already used** for pairing token verification elsewhere in the codebase — just missed for TLS fingerprints.

```diff
- if (fingerprint !== expected) {
+ if (!safeEqualSecret(fingerprint, expected)) {
```

## Why safeEqualSecret and not raw timingSafeEqual

`timingSafeEqual` requires both buffers to have equal length, which would leak the length of the expected fingerprint. `safeEqualSecret` avoids this by hashing both values with SHA-256 first (producing fixed 32-byte digests), then comparing the digests in constant time.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tsgo` — compiles cleanly
- [x] `pnpm check` — lint/format passes
- [x] Existing `safeEqualSecret` tests in `src/security/audit-extra.sync.test.ts` cover equal, unequal, different-length, and undefined inputs
- [x] No remaining `fingerprint !== expected` patterns in codebase

target.title: fix: keep Codex delegation controls directly available
target.body:
Closes #99464
Related: #99561

AI-assisted. This branch preserves the original #99561 commits by @100yenadmin and adjusts the final behavior to the independently validated fix direction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server users could be told that deferred OpenClaw delegation tools were searchable, but an explicit `tool_search` for `sessions_spawn` did not make the OpenClaw tool callable. The model could then answer without spawning the requested child session.

It also avoids changing the registered `heartbeat_respond` schema between normal and heartbeat turns on a resumed Codex thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the small, stable OpenClaw control set (`agents_list`, `sessions_spawn`, and `sessions_yield`) directly available on every Codex app-server turn. Broad tools remain deferred behind `tool_search`, and `heartbeat_respond` remains deferred with a stable registration across normal and heartbeat turns.

This keeps delegation controls reliable without making the entire OpenClaw tool catalog direct, and preserves the Codex app-server requirement that a resumed thread retain the same registered dynamic-tool definitions.

## User Impact

Codex app-server agents can reliably list agents, spawn subagents, and yield without depending on connector-oriented `tool_search` resolution. Existing deferred-tool behavior remains in place for the broader catalog, and heartbeat turns no longer risk a thread schema mismatch.

target.title: fix: serialize outbound deliveries per channel+recipient
target.body:
## Summary

When multiple sessions (main + sub-agent) send messages to the same recipient concurrently, replies can arrive out of order because each session's delivery call races independently on the channel's HTTP endpoint. Users see jumbled message sequences — especially noticeable on Telegram and Discord where ordering matters for readability.

**Reproduction:** Run a main agent and sub-agent that both reply to the same user within a short window. Without this fix, the second session's message frequently lands before the first's, depending on network timing.

**Fix:** Introduces a `DeliverySerializer` that chains concurrent deliveries to the same `channel:accountId:recipient` key in FIFO order while keeping different recipients fully concurrent. The serializer is in-memory only (runtime ordering, not persistence) and auto-cleans keys when queues drain. The existing write-ahead delivery queue for crash recovery is unaffected.

A follow-up commit wraps `fn()` in `Promise.resolve().then()` so a synchronous throw is converted to a rejection rather than hanging the result promise forever (addresses review feedback).

Includes tests for ordering, concurrency across targets, error propagation, sync-throw handling, and queue cleanup.

Rebased to 2026.3.13.

---

## Real behavior proof — Telegram, live session (2026-05-22)

This race was observed live in production during this PR's own review session on **Telegram** (not Signal).

**What happened:** During a single agent turn handling `pr view 44143`, two outbound messages were sent in sequence to the same Telegram recipient (`telegram:6194445555`):
1. A long ClawSweeper analysis dump (~4KB)
2. A summary message referencing and synthesizing that analysis

**Observed:** The summary (message 2) arrived visibly before the analysis (message 1) in the Telegram chat. The recipient had to read the synthesis before the content it was synthesizing — the exact inversion this PR fixes.

**Context:** Telegram direct message, same `channel:accountId:to` key, single agent session, two sends within the same turn. No sub-agent involved — the race can happen within a single session turn when one send is large enough to lose the HTTP timing race against a smaller follow-up send.

**Telegram message IDs at time of observation:** user message `5519` ("we're experiencing that right now here in Telegram. Look at your last 3 messages"), preceded by the two inverted agent messages. Timestamp: 2026-05-22 ~15:00 EDT.

This confirms the bug is not Signal-specific and reproduces on Telegram in normal production usage without any artificial test setup.

target.title: fix: outbound recovery can replay already sent replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users relying on outbound delivery recovery could have an already sent reply replayed when recovery successfully sent the message but post-send bookkeeping or an adapter commit hook failed.

The affected workflow is outbound delivery recovery after a restart or failed send attempt. Once the platform send succeeds, the recovery entry must not remain as an ordinary pending retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery now marks sent replay attempts as `unknown_after_send` before acknowledging the pending queue entry, matching the live send invariant. Commit-hook failures are still isolated, but the runner returns diagnostics so recovery can persist a failed diagnostic row without requeuing the sent delivery.

## User Impact

Recovered outbound messages no longer remain pending for replay after recovery has evidence that the platform send succeeded. Operators also get a failed diagnostic row for post-send failures instead of losing the diagnostic state.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` — 24 tests passed.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts` — 12 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:test-types` — passed.
- `npx oxlint --deny=warn --ignore-path=.oxlintignore src/infra/outbound/delivery-commit-hooks.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` — passed.
- Manual recovery proof with a successful recovered send and throwing commit hook:


target.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier
target.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: tiered bootstrap loading — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) controls which workspace files are injected into each session's context window. Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

Real environment tested: macOS 26.2 on Apple Silicon, Node 24.13.0, pnpm 11.2.2, against the fork branch tip at commit `5cdaf8e774`. A reproduction harness at the repo root (`repro-tiered-bootstrap.mts`, not committed) imports the real `src/agents/workspace.ts` from this branch and invokes `resolveBootstrapTier` and `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` against an explicit `WorkspaceBootstrapFile[]` containing both root-loaded files and hook-loaded extras whose basenames collide with the root allowlist.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `git checkout 5cdaf8e774` (this PR's head)
2. `pnpm install --prefer-offline --frozen-lockfile`
3. Author the reproduction harness at the repo root, importing `./src/agents/workspace.js` and calling the exported functions directly with a `WorkspaceBootstrapFile[]` shaped like a real workspace (root files + two hook-sourced `packages/*/AGENTS.md` entries).
4. `node ./node_modules/.bin/tsx repro-tiered-bootstrap.mts`

## What Problem This Solves

The `gateway-smoke`, `mcp-gateway-connect-startup-retry`, and `mcp-plugin-tools-call` QA scenarios claimed Gateway/MCP behavior from helper-level or in-memory tests instead of exercising the real process and transport boundaries.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuses the existing QA Gateway child fixture and adds an `onListening` lifecycle hook so a client can start after the real socket binds but before Gateway readiness.
- Runs `gateway-smoke` against a real Gateway child and its real WebSocket/health surfaces.
- Starts a real MCP stdio client before Gateway readiness. A fixture-plugin startup gate is released only after a recording proxy observes the real connect frame, deterministically exercising the production startup-unavailable retry response and protocol negotiation.
- Registers a fixture plugin, starts the real plugin-tools stdio server, lists its tools, and calls `memory_search` with the MCP SDK client.
- Converts all three scenario definitions to canonical script evidence with primary coverage.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. QA evidence now fails when the real Gateway or MCP process, readiness, retry, negotiation, plugin discovery, stdio transport, or tool invocation boundary regresses.

## Evidence

- Real scenario producers:
  - `gateway-smoke`: pass

target.title: fix(diagnostic): avoid model-call stream hot-path object copies
target.body:
Related: #91588
Related: #97211

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where diagnostic model-call event accounting still copies stream chunks and model-call event bases with object rest/spread on hot paths. Issue #91588 includes field evidence that points at V8 dictionary-mode `CopyDataProperties` work around the diagnostic stream byte-accounting path during long-running Gateway workloads.

Scope boundary: This PR only addresses diagnostic model-call stream copy/spread hot paths; it does not close the broader Gateway RSS/OOM tracker or prove a multi-day RSS plateau.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change removes object rest from `responseStreamChunkByteLengthUnchecked()` and conditional object spreads from `baseModelCallEvent()` while keeping the same diagnostic event fields. The stream copy now uses a null-prototype target so an own enumerable `__proto__` stream-chunk field remains a data key instead of interacting with `Object.prototype` behavior.

This PR is ready for review for the narrow diagnostic hot-path mitigation because validation now covers focused regression behavior plus inspectable current-head runtime proof. Longer-running Gateway RSS proof remains outside this submission's current evidence.

## User Impact

Operators running long-lived Gateway sessions should get less diagnostic hot-path object-copy churn during model-call streaming. The change is diagnostic-internal and does not intentionally alter model responses, provider transport, or persisted session data.

## Breaking changes (if any)

None expected.

## Implementation

- Replace `{ partial, ...snapshotlessChunk }` on stream chunks with direct JSON byte accounting for own enumerable fields except `partial`, avoiding a snapshotless chunk allocation on the normal non-`toJSON` path while preserving JSON omission behavior for unsupported values.
- Preserve object-property `JSON.stringify` semantics for non-partial values, including value-level `toJSON(key)` for object/function values and monkey-patched BigInt values, by serializing through a one-property null-prototype wrapper instead of as root values.
- Preserve root `JSON.stringify` semantics when a stream chunk exposes callable `toJSON` via own non-enumerable or inherited/prototype lookup: a rare proxy path hides `partial` lazily, and a descriptor-preserving fallback handles non-configurable/non-extensible shapes.
- Keep own enumerable `__proto__` chunk fields as JSON-serializable data keys without mutating `Object.prototype`, including the `toJSON` snapshot fallback path.
- Build `baseModelCallEvent()` once and assign optional fields conditionally instead of using conditional spread literals.
- Add regression coverage for partial getter safety, value-level `toJSON(key)`, BigInt `toJSON(key)`, callable chunk-level `toJSON`, lazy getter ordering, non-configurable `partial` fallback, and own enumerable `__proto__` data-key preservation.

## Labels considered

`P0`, `impact:session-state`, `impact:message-loss`, `impact:crash-loop`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:needs-live-repro`, and `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` from #91588 were considered when setting this PR's narrow scope and proof strategy.

## Validation

Current PR head: `7c500070c700e1df312529722553885476da8a73`
Proof baseline commit: `28a841472684eed2d98a1a277fcefc30855b580b`

Current-head GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof:

- Latest proof run: `PR 99154 model diagnostic runtime proof` — passed: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28677737053
- Latest artifact: `pr99154-model-diagnostic-runtime-proof-28677737053-1` (`summary.md`, `baseline.json`, and `head.json`).
- Environment: GitHub Actions, `ubuntu-24.04`, Node `v24.18.0`, `workflow_dispatch`.
- Head binding: artifact `head.json` records `commit=7c500070c700e1df312529722553885476da8a73`, matching the current PR head. The workflow wrapper branch commit is not used as the proof binding source.
- Supporting repeat run on the same PR head also passed: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28677394470 with artifact `pr99154-model-diagnostic-runtime-proof-28677394470-1`.

Latest proof run edge behavior:

- Baseline partial-getter edge failed as expected: expected `34` bytes, actual byte count absent, `partialReads=1`.
- PR head partial-getter edge passed: expected/actual `34` bytes, `partialReads=0`.
- PR head own non-enumerable chunk `toJSON` proxy edge passed: expected/actual `54` bytes, `partialReads=0`, unrelated throwing getter reads `0`.
- PR head inherited/prototype chunk `toJSON` proxy edge passed: expected/actual `35` bytes.
- PR head non-configurable `partial` snapshot fallback edge passed: expected/actual `54` bytes, unrelated throwing getter reads `0`, `objectPrototypeClean=true`.
- PR head own enumerable `__proto__` data-key edge passed: expected/actual `73` bytes, `objectPrototypeClean=true`.
- PR head value-level `toJSON(key)` edge passed: expected/actual `68` bytes, observed key `value`.
- PR head BigInt `toJSON(key)` edge passed: expected/actual `52` bytes, observed key `value`.

Latest proof run synthetic model-call stream benchmark:

- 50,000 representative non-delta stream chunks were drained through `wrapStreamFnWithDiagnosticModelCallEvents()`.
- Baseline and PR head both reported `responseStreamBytes=2911669`, so the diagnostic byte-accounting contract stayed stable.
- Latest run duration: baseline `159.92 ms`, PR head `183.04 ms`; supporting repeat duration: baseline `196.80 ms`, PR head `189.29 ms`. Runtime duration is therefore recorded as short-run signal only, not used as a stable speedup claim.

Latest proof run large partial-getter benchmark:

- 10,000 chunks with large accumulated `partial` snapshots.
- Baseline `partialReads=10000`; PR head `partialReads=0`.
- Baseline duration `39.88 ms`; PR head duration `39.41 ms`.
- Baseline and PR head both reported expected/actual bytes `527780 / 527780` on the PR head byte-accounting path.

GitHub Actions/check read-back on current PR head:

- Workflow-level current-head rollup completed successfully for the visible PR workflows: `CI`, `CodeQL`, `CodeQL Critical Quality`, `OpenGrep — PR Diff`, `Workflow Sanity`, `iOS Periphery Dead Code`, `Real behavior proof`, `Dependency Guard`, `Security Sensitive Guard`, `Labeler`, `Auto response`, and `ClawSweeper Dispatch`.
- Representative current-head runs:
  - `CI`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677356289
  - `CodeQL`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677356252
  - `CodeQL Critical Quality`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677356260
  - `OpenGrep — PR Diff`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677356263
  - `Workflow Sanity`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677356275
  - `Real behavior proof`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677355555
- Check-run read-back for `7c500070c700e1df312529722553885476da8a73`: `66` success, `29` skipped, `1` neutral, `0` failed, `0` pending.

## Evidence source map

- Issue field evidence: #91588 contains public native stack evidence around V8 `Runtime_CopyDataPropertiesWithExcludedPropertiesOnStack` / dictionary-key collection and identifies the diagnostic stream chunk copy site.
- Current-head GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28677737053 compares the baseline commit and current PR head with a 50,000-chunk model-call diagnostic stream workload, a 10,000-chunk large-partial getter workload, and edge checks for partial snapshots, value-level `toJSON(key)`, BigInt `toJSON(key)`, callable chunk-level `toJSON`, lazy getter ordering, non-configurable `partial`, and own enumerable `__proto__` data keys.
- Supporting current-head repeat proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28677394470 passed on the same PR head and independently confirms the edge checks plus 50,000-chunk synthetic stream byte-equivalence.
- Regression tests: `attempt.model-diagnostic-events.test.ts` covers partial snapshot exclusion without reading `partial`, value-level `toJSON(key)`, BigInt `toJSON(key)`, own non-enumerable/prototype chunk `toJSON` behavior, non-configurable `partial` fallback, unrelated lazy getters, and own enumerable `__proto__` data-key byte accounting.
- GitHub Actions/checks: current-head PR workflows completed successfully with no failed or pending check runs in the status rollup.

## Data model / migration compatibility

No persistent data model or runtime storage schema is changed. The modified runtime file constructs transient model-call diagnostic events and diagnostic byte counts; it does not change serialized session-state schemas, vector/embedding metadata, migrations, stores, or upgrade code. The test-file additions exercise in-memory diagnostic event byte accounting only.

## Risk

- Diagnostic byte accounting can be sensitive to unusual provider stream chunk shapes. The added tests and proof cover the relevant review edges: skipping `partial` without reading it, object-property value `toJSON(key)`, BigInt `toJSON(key)`, callable chunk-level `toJSON` lookup/ordering, non-configurable `partial` fallback, and own enumerable `__proto__` data keys.
- The normal non-`toJSON` chunk path remains allocation-conscious: primitive values serialize directly, while object/function values and BigInt values use one small wrapper only when needed to preserve object-property serialization semantics.
- Current-head timing across two short synthetic runs is mixed, so this PR should be evaluated as a focused allocation/read-avoidance and byte-semantics mitigation rather than as broad performance proof.
- This does not address diagnostic maps, session retention, plugin retention, or other long-running RSS contributors discussed in #91588.
- The implementation avoids provider/runtime behavior changes and is limited to diagnostic event construction and byte accounting.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. No data migration, config migration, or persisted format change is involved.

## Docs updated

No documentation files were changed. The patch is limited to diagnostic implementation code plus focused regression tests.

## Related issue / PR

- Related: #91588
- Related: #97211

#97211 covers the same diagnostic hot path and has public review feedback around proof, scope, and `__proto__` behavior. This PR carries focused regression tests and uses non-closing issue references so it does not auto-close the broader Gateway RSS/OOM tracker.

## Review context addressed

- ClawSweeper requested inspectable real behavior proof before merge. The PR body now includes current-head GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof and artifact details in Validation.
- ClawSweeper flagged stale proof/head mismatch in the previous review. The latest artifact records `commit=7c500070c700e1df312529722553885476da8a73`, matching the current PR head.
- ClawSweeper flagged persistent data-model compatibility proof as a merge concern. The Data model / migration compatibility section now states the exact persistence boundary: transient diagnostic event construction only, with no serialized session-state, vector/embedding metadata, migration, store, or upgrade-code change.
- Review feedback flagged that the earlier byte counter bypassed callable chunk-level `toJSON` semantics. The implementation now preserves root `JSON.stringify` callable `toJSON` lookup for own non-enumerable and inherited/prototype methods while hiding `partial`.
